name: Ḥayyim Yosef David Azulai, the Ḥida (1724–1806)
desc: The author of the diary. In the diary itself he writes "I", which is not indexed; the hits are the editors' parts.

name: Rachel, the Ḥida's first wife
desc: Died on 20 Sivan 5533 (11 June 1773); the news reached him in Tunis.

name: Rachel, the Ḥida's second wife
desc: Married in Pisa on 7 Ḥeshvan 5539 (28 October 1778). Perhaps of the family of Signor Raphael of Pisa.

name: Abraham Azulai, the Ḥida's son
desc: Came from Tunis in 1783 and from Algiers in 1785 to the lazaretto of Livorno.

name: Isaiah Azulai, the Ḥida's son
desc: Cantor in Ancona; father of R. Moses Azulai. In 1777 he wrote that he wanted to join his father.

name: Sarah, the Ḥida's daughter
desc: Named after his mother; married to a gevir in Livorno. Her husband is probably the "gevir, my son-in-law" who met the Ḥida at Livorno in 1778.

name: Moses Azulai, the Ḥida's grandson
desc: Son of R. Isaiah; the source of most stories in Shem Tov. R. Abraham Ḥai Musafia heard them from him in Ancona in 1843–44. The grandson in whose hands the editor's preface places the manuscript.

name: Raphael Isaac Zeraḥiah Azulai, the Ḥida's father

patterns.rx: R\. Isaac(?=, of blessed memory, the father)

desc: Sent his son from Jerusalem to Hebron after a dream. Author of the novellae Zera Yitzḥak.

name: Isaiah, the Ḥida's great-grandfather
desc: Wrote the small Megillah that was stolen and returned.

name: Abraham Azulai (d. 1643)
desc: Kabbalist of Hebron, author of Ḥesed le-Avraham; ancestor of the Ḥida.

name: Moses and Judah, the Ḥida's brothers-in-law
desc: With him in Tunis when the news of his wife's death came.

name: Moses ben Meir
desc: A young man with the Ḥida in Tunis when the news of his wife's death came.

name: Y. Valle
desc: Probably the author of notes on the Shulḥan Arukh that the Ḥida saw in Modena.

name: The Ḥida's son-in-law in Livorno
desc: A gevir of Livorno; probably the husband of his daughter Sarah.

name: Abraham Gabbai, the Ḥida's servant
desc: Travelled with him; his conduct in Amsterdam and Paris angered the Ḥida, and they parted in Turin in 1778.

name: Abraham Ḥai Musafia
desc: Rabbi; saw the manuscript of the diary in Ancona and passed on the family stories printed in Shem Tov.

name: Joseph Shabbetai Farḥi (1802–1882)
desc: Of Livorno; the "young man" who copied the manuscript and published the Livorno printing (Ben Amozegh, 1879). He signs ישפ"ה.

name: Samuel, a gevir
desc: Very ill in Sivan 1773, before the Ḥida sailed for Tunis.

name: Abraham Tayyib
desc: Rabbi in Tunis, with many disciples.

name: Joseph Zarqa
desc: Rabbi and scribe in Tunis, with about sixty disciples.

name: Abraham Katan
desc: Disciple of Joseph Zarqa in Tunis.

name: Jacob Ma'arek
desc: Disciple of Joseph Zarqa in Tunis.

name: Joseph Bashmut
desc: Scholar in Tunis who studied with the Ḥida.

name: Solomon Nataf, the qaid
desc: A qaid (Jewish leader) in Tunis; the Ḥida dined with him one day in 1774, and the rabbis were there.

name: Leon Capi
desc: Of Livorno; sent chocolate to the lazaretto.

name: Pereira family of Livorno
patterns: Signor Gabriel and Signor Jacob Pereira
desc: Close friends of the Ḥida. He lived in the house of Signor Pereira in Livorno, and his yahrzeit was kept in the Pereira yeshivah.

name: Y. Algazi
desc: Isaac Algazi, sage of Livorno; in 1774 he came every day to the Ḥida in the lazaretto and sent him pan esponjado.

name: Y. Polacco
desc: The Ḥida's friend in Livorno, who held his books and bonds; died 1774.

name: Yom Tov Algazi
desc: Sage of Jerusalem; came to Livorno in 1775. Probably also the "R. Yom Tov A." who fled from Jerusalem to Safed in 1776.

name: Jacob le-Vet Ḥazan
desc: Sage of Jerusalem who came to Livorno with Yom Tov Algazi in 1775.

name: Y. Meyuḥas
desc: Sage of Jerusalem who fled to Safed after a quarrel.

name: Jacob Ḥai Levi
desc: Rabbi in Florence, an old friend from Venice.

name: Shalom Tzaddik
desc: The Ḥida was sandak for his son Joseph Ḥayyim, 1775.

name: Moses Foa
desc: Rabbinic judge in Senigallia.

name: Phinehas ha-Kohen
desc: Gevir of Ancona, son of Abraham ha-Kohen; the Ḥida's host there.

name: Joel Ḥamitz
desc: Given the title maskil and made cantor of the Sephardi congregation of Ancona, 1776.

name: Abraham Jona
desc: Scholar in Venice; read the Birkei Yosef with the Ḥida every day.

name: Daniel Tolentino of Ragusa
desc: Took the Ḥida round Venice, 1776.

name: Menaḥem Ashkenazi of Constantinople
desc: Took the Ḥida to the Arsenal of Venice.

name: Gad Foa
patterns: Gad son of the honored Samuel Foa
desc: Ran the Bragadin Hebrew press in Venice; a friend of the Ḥida.

name: Bragadin
desc: Venetian nobleman who owned the Hebrew press.

name: Solomon Pazini
desc: Of Venice, with his son Mordecai.

name: Almeida family of Venice
patterns: Abraham son of Kalonymus Joseph Ḥai
Abraham, son of Kalonymus Joseph Ḥai
desc: The Ḥida was sandak for Abraham son of Kalonymus Joseph Ḥai, grandson of Abraham Franco Almeida (1776), and for the son of Solomon Franco de Almeida (1777).

name: Jacob Ḥayyim Bivante
patterns: Jacob Ḥayyim Bivante son of Judah
desc: Gevir of the Levantine congregation of Venice.

name: Rabbi Calimani
desc: Rabbi in Venice.

desc: Great gevir of Venice.

name: Daniel Bonfil
desc: Great gevir of Venice.

name: David Uziel
desc: Of Venice; his wife was the sister of Signor Godica.

name: Ḥayyim ha-Levi of Bosnia
desc: Gevir in Venice, where the Ḥida spent Friday nights.

name: Abraham Curiel
patterns: R\. Abraham son of the honored R\. Menaḥem Curiel
desc: Gevir and sage in Venice.

name: Jacob Burla
desc: Probably the sage R. Y. B. of Venice, 1776: an emissary of Jerusalem, in Livorno with Yom Tov Algazi in 1775.

name: Moia
desc: Old scribe in Venice.

name: Vidal Angel
desc: Gevir in Venice.

name: Menaḥem Vivante
desc: Of Venice.

name: Ishmael ha-Kohen
desc: Rabbi in Modena. The Ḥida disputed his rulings, among them one on inoculation.

name: Sanguinetti family of Modena
patterns: Signor Azariah son of Abraham Nethanel Sanguinetti

name: Mordecai Carmi
desc: Travelled with the Ḥida to Avignon, 1777.

R\. Moses son of Joseph de Roquemartine
desc: Warden of Carpentras and the Ḥida's friend there in 1755; in July 1777 his host, who went with him to Avignon and later spoke hard words over the mission. name: Bagaio
desc: An earlier emissary, whose demands had turned Avignon against the mission.

name: Elijah Reuel
desc: Of Avignon.

name: Abraham Gradis
desc: Merchant of Bordeaux.

name: Jacob Cusin
desc: Of Trieste, grandson of Marco Levi; the Ḥida's host.

name: Y. Formiggini
desc: Rabbi in Trieste.

name: Marco Levi
desc: Head of the community of Trieste.

name: David Levi
patterns: Signor David son of Kalman ha-Levi
desc: Of Trieste, grandson of Marco Levi.

name: Lapdon
desc: Warden in Trieste.

name: Treves of Trieste
desc: Warden in Trieste.

name: Joachim Arsil
desc: Of Trieste.

name: Fabri
desc: Learned gentile of the Académie des Sciences in Paris, interested in kabbalah; took the Ḥida to the royal library and to Versailles.

name: Mordecai Ventura
desc: Grammarian and linguist in Paris who accompanied the Ḥida.

name: Elijah Perpignan
desc: Of Paris; the Ḥida made peace between him and his wife.

name: Moses Perpignan
desc: Of Paris.

name: Abraham Vidal
desc: Of Paris.

name: Marquis de Thomé
desc: French scholar interested in kabbalah, who asked the Ḥida's blessing.

name: Marquise de Croix
desc: Noblewoman of Paris who said she saw angels and spirits.

name: Comte de Provence
desc: Brother of Louis XVI, later King Louis XVIII.

name: Comte d'Artois
desc: Brother of Louis XVI, later King Charles X.

name: Louis XVI, King of France
desc: The Ḥida saw him pass at Versailles in January 1778.

name: Comte de Maillebois
desc: Marshal of France; gave the Ḥida letters of recommendation.

name: Baal Shem of London (Samuel Jacob Falk)
desc: Kabbalist in London, whom the Ḥida blamed for revealing practical kabbalah to the nobility.

name: Madame Adélaïde
desc: Aunt of Louis XVI; gave the Ḥida a letter to her niece in Turin.

name: Prince of Piedmont
desc: Heir of the King of Sardinia, married to the sister of Louis XVI.

name: Rast
desc: Physician in Paris who came with a priest and a list of questions.

name: David Ḥayyim Ariani
desc: The Ḥida's travelling companion from Italy to Turin; ill in Paris in August 1778.

name: Eizik
desc: Remembered the Ḥida from his first mission, on the road to Amsterdam.

name: Abraham Ze'evi
desc: Emissary to Germany, in Amsterdam in 1778.

name: Solomon Shalem
desc: Rabbi of the Portuguese community of Amsterdam. He came from Izmir; the Ḥida found him cold and sometimes hostile.

name: Saul Löwenstamm

name: Leib Hirsch
desc: Scholar in Amsterdam.

name: Gomez
desc: Cantor in Amsterdam.

name: Isaac Teixeira de Mattos
desc: Gevir in Amsterdam, the Ḥida's friend.

name: Moses Alvares
desc: Of Amsterdam, brother of Solomon of Bayonne; his son Joseph was the son-in-law of Rabbi Shalem.

name: Medina
desc: Of Amsterdam.

name: Isaac Bueno de Mesquita
desc: Of Amsterdam. Signor Mesquita on Purim 1778 may be another member of the family.

name: David ha-Kohen
desc: Of Amsterdam; sent the Ḥida the Ezat Sofer Pentateuch.

name: Aaron Capadose
desc: Gevir of Amsterdam, one of the padrinos of the mission.

name: Isaac ben Dana
desc: Of Amsterdam.

name: Isaac ben Dana de Brito
desc: Sage of Amsterdam. After his death the community invited the Ḥida to succeed him, and he declined.

name: Ḥayyim Abulafia
desc: Rabbi; invited to Amsterdam while in Salonika, but went to Izmir.

name: Britano
desc: Gentile of Amsterdam.

name: Ebelsman
desc: Gentile of Amsterdam, who gave the Ḥida chocolate made in his house.

name: Isaac Gutierrez
desc: Of Amsterdam.

name: Moses de Isaac Suasso
patterns: Signor Moses de Isaac Israel Suasso
desc: Gevir of Amsterdam, one of the padrinos of the mission.

name: Baron Suasso
desc: Of The Hague; showed the Ḥida a tiny Torah scroll and Megillah.

name: Azevedo
desc: Of Amsterdam.

name: Benjamin
desc: Of Amsterdam.

name: Aaron Lombroso
desc: Of Amsterdam; his wife died in April 1778.

name: Ẓevi (Hirsch) of Bolechów

desc: Told the stories of R. Heschel and the Shakh.

name: Carlo Birnandi
desc: Gentile merchant of Amsterdam (printed also Widenandi), who gave the Ḥida letters of recommendation to London and Turin; Freimann reads both forms as Birnandi.

name: Kalonymus
desc: Accompanied the Ḥida from Amsterdam to The Hague.

name: Solomon Saruk
desc: Ḥazzan in The Hague.

name: Saul Segal
desc: Rabbi in The Hague, brother-in-law of R. Saul of Amsterdam.

name: Moses de Pinto
desc: Of The Hague.

name: Tobias Boas
desc: Banker of The Hague, eighty-three years old in 1778.

name: Ezekiel, Moses Lehren and Simeon Zimir
desc: Went with the Ḥida to Rotterdam; Ezekiel and Simeon Zimir were cantors.

name: Moses Springer
desc: Won the lottery, he said, by the Ḥida's blessing.

name: Isaac Segal Leiden
desc: Of The Hague; the Ḥida blessed his childless wife.

name: Samuel Peixotto
desc: Of Bordeaux; tried to divorce his wife against her will, and his advocate attacked the Ḥida in print.

name: Lipman Calmer
desc: Behind the printed attack on the Ḥida.

name: Raphael of Pisa
desc: The Ḥida's host in Pisa in 1778; probably the father or a near kinsman of his second wife (see the note there).

name: Ferridas
desc: Of Livorno.

name: Miranda

name: Abraham Judah Faro
desc: Of Livorno.

desc: Gevir of Livorno, in whose yeshivah the Ḥida preached.

name: Acciaioli family of Livorno
patterns: Signori Aaron, Judah and David Acciaioli
desc: Joined the Ḥida for the Seder in Livorno, 1785.

name: David Yekutiel ha-Kohen
desc: Emissary and old scholar of Jerusalem.

name: Isaac Lombroso
desc: Rabbi in Tunis.

name: Lombroso of Livorno
desc: Gevir who held the Ḥida's legacy of 1,500 thalers; later bankrupt.

name: Ḥayyim Alamia
desc: Brought back the stolen Megillah to R. Isaiah Azulai.

name: Samuel Alamia
desc: Of Ancona; the Ḥida was sandak for his son, 1776.

name: Solomon Moses Cavaliero
desc: Of Ferrara; the Ḥida was sandak for his son, 1776.

name: Ḥayyim Vital (1542–1620)
desc: Disciple of the Ari.

name: Menaḥem ha-Meiri

desc: Kabbalist of Safed, author of Or Yakar.

desc: Kabbalist; his book of kavvanot was among the manuscripts in Modena.

desc: Author of Matsref la-Ḥokhmah.

desc: Kabbalist; buried in Mantua.

desc: Earlier rabbi in Modena.

desc: Earlier rabbi and teacher in Modena.

name: Elijah Shapira
desc: Died in Tunis while praying.

name: Moses Mizraḥi
desc: Rabbi of Jerusalem; the Ḥida saw him in a dream.

name: Isaac Israeli
desc: Author of Yesod Olam.

name: Isaiah di Trani
desc: His notes on the Pentateuch, in the royal library in Paris, were copied by the Ḥida.

desc: Signed in agreement on the case of the mamzer who purified his seed.

desc: Rabbi in Vienna, author of Vavei ha-Amudim.

desc: An elder of Lippiano with whom the Ḥida lodged.

desc: A qatzin of Pesaro at whose house the Ḥida spent the Sabbath.

name: Abraham, head of the community of Kriegshaber
desc: Head of the community of Kriegshaber; he turned against the Ḥida after a letter from Leib of Pfersee.

name: Wolf of Wassertrüdingen, warden of the province of Ansbach
desc: A pious scholar who received the Ḥida in Wassertrüdingen.

name: Joseph, judge of the province of Ansbach
desc: Son-in-law of Wolf of Wassertrüdingen; the Ḥida debated with him for six hours and saw his novellae on Horayot.

name: Ḥayyim, parnas of Bechhofen
desc: A hard parnas of Bechhofen who gave one reichstaler.

name: Heschel, rabbi of the province of Ansbach
desc: The provincial rabbi at Lehrberg, who said he recognized none of the Ḥida's signatures.

name: David of Ansbach
desc: A man in Ansbach who recognized one of the signatures.

name: Zechariah Kleve of Fürth
desc: A notable of Fürth who revealed the Ḥida's secret letter about Judah Yeruḥam to the parnasim.

name: Judah Yeruḥam, emissary
desc: An emissary who had made a settlement in Fürth for the whole Land of Israel; the Ḥida carried a letter of the rabbis of Hebron against him.

name: Zanvil of Niederwerrn
desc: A rich notable of Niederwerrn who gave a quarter of a florin.

name: Aaron of Arnstein
desc: A notable of Arnstein who would not let the Ḥida enter the town.

name: Leib son of Baruch Rapoport, rabbi of Heidingsfeld
patterns: R\. Leib son of our teacher R\. Baruch Rapoport
desc: The rabbi of Heidingsfeld, who showed the Ḥida a friendly face.

name: Leib of Seligenstadt
desc: A notable of Seligenstadt who did the Ḥida much kindness.

name: Isaac, rabbi of Hanau
desc: Head of the court of Hanau, son-in-law of Hillman of Metz; at first he did not trust the signatures, then wrote for the Ḥida.

name: Wolf, head of the court of Kałuszyn
desc: Brother of Isaac, the rabbi of Hanau; he was with him in Hanau.

name: Meir Worms, parnas of Frankfurt
desc: The new parnas of Frankfurt to whom Wolf Hintel brought the Ḥida.

name: Wolf Hintel of Hamburg
desc: A young scholar who met the Ḥida at the harbour of Frankfurt and became his close friend; he died in the fire in Reuben Scheyer's house.

name: Leib Wetzlar of Frankfurt
desc: A learned householder of Frankfurt in whose house the Ḥida lodged for more than three months.

name: Reuben Scheyer Segal, parnas of Frankfurt
desc: A rich parnas of Frankfurt who honoured the Ḥida; his house burned on Ḥanukkah 1754 and he died soon after. Spelled Scheyer and Scheuer.

name: Judah Scheyer Segal, son of Reuben Scheyer
desc: The only son of Reuben Scheyer; he survived the fire and sent the Ḥida the mission's money.

name: Moses Lopez Pereira, Baron d'Aguilar, of Vienna
desc: A nobleman in Vienna to whom the Ḥida wrote to confirm his mission.

name: Jacob Joshua Falk, author of Pnei Yehoshua, rabbi of Frankfurt
desc: The av bet din of Frankfurt, living in Worms because of the dispute; he confirmed the signatures and wrote a letter for the Ḥida. Father of the Baal Shem of London.

name: Isaac ha-Kohen of Jerusalem, author of Batei Kehunah
desc: A rabbi of Jerusalem who cited the Pnei Yehoshua in his book Batei Kehunah.

name: The author of Panim Me'irot (Meir Eisenstadt)
desc: The Ḥida answered one of his difficulties on the basis of the Pnei Yehoshua.

name: Jonathan Eybeschütz, rabbi of Prague and of Altona, Hamburg and Wandsbek
desc: The rabbi at the centre of the amulet dispute, of which the Pnei Yehoshua told the Ḥida in Worms. R. Ẓevi of Bolechów was his disciple, and so the Ashkenazim of Amsterdam ignored that sage.

name: Jacob Emden (Jacob son of Ẓevi Hirsch)
desc: He raised the outcry against Jonathan Eybeschütz's amulets.

name: Shabbetai Tzevi
desc: The false messiah; Eybeschütz's opponents said he held his faith. Probably the 'Sh. Ts.' whose picture Meir Rovigo showed the Ḥida.

name: Joseph Sasson, scribe of Constantinople
desc: The Ḥida recognized his style in the letter of the rabbis of Constantinople.

name: Eleazar of Worms (Garmiza), the Rokeaḥ
desc: A native of Worms.

name: Maharam of Rothenburg (Meir of Rothenburg)
desc: Said to be buried in Worms.

name: Rabbenu Samson of Sens
desc: The old Talmud manuscript at Pfersee was written in Paris for one of his relatives.

name: David Meldola, sage of Amsterdam
desc: A sage of Amsterdam who kept the Ḥida's letters, met him at Amersfoort and lodged him, but harmed his mission to sell his own books. Came to The Hague to marry off his daughter; spoke against Shalem and told the story of the Peri Ḥadash in Amsterdam.

name: Süsskind Stern of Frankfurt
desc: A dignitary of Frankfurt; the Ḥida spent a Sabbath with him.

name: Michael Speyer of Frankfurt
desc: A dignitary of Frankfurt; the Ḥida spent two Sabbaths with him.

name: Baer Kann of Frankfurt am Main
desc: A dignitary of Frankfurt; the Ḥida spent a Sabbath with him. "The great notable of Frankfurt am Main", father of Eliezer Kann.

name: Meir Hanover of Frankfurt
desc: A dignitary of Frankfurt; the Ḥida spent a Sabbath with him.

name: Zozel Kulp of Frankfurt
desc: A dignitary of Frankfurt; the Ḥida spent a Sabbath with him.

name: Nathan Kulp of Frankfurt
desc: A dignitary of Frankfurt; the Ḥida spent a Sabbath with him.

name: Israel, scribe of Frankfurt
desc: The community scribe of Frankfurt, who wrote in the register that the gift was for the Ashkenazim.

name: Moses Rapp, rabbi in Frankfurt
desc: A rabbi in Frankfurt who wrote the Ḥida a letter of recommendation.

name: Eizik Gundersheim of Mainz
desc: A dignitary of Mainz with whom the Ḥida lodged.

name: Israel of Bingen
desc: A holy and pious scholar whom the Ḥida saw in Bingen.

name: Bendit Gumpel of Nijmegen
desc: A famous qatzin, father of Feibelman of Cleve and Elia of Nijmegen.

name: Feibelman of Cleve, son of Bendit Gumpel
desc: A qatzin of Cleve who lodged the Ḥida in royal rooms.

name: Elia son of Bendit, parnas of Nijmegen
patterns: R\. Elia son of R\. Bendit
desc: Brother of Feibelman; the Ḥida lodged with him in Nijmegen.

name: Gitli, the Ḥida's aunt in Cleve
desc: His mother's half-sister, daughter of Joseph Bialer, wife of Falk son of Nathanel; she told him the family's descent.

name: Joseph Bialer, the Ḥida's grandfather
desc: His mother's father, a pious kabbalist who came to Jerusalem with Judah Ḥasid.

name: Judah Ḥasid
desc: The holy rabbi with whose company Joseph Bialer came to Jerusalem about sixty years before.

name: Joshua Falk, author of the Derishah and the Sema

patterns.rx: R\. Falk(?= of blessed memory, author)

desc: The Ḥida asked his aunt how the family was related to him.

name: Judah, son or grandson of the Sema
desc: An ancestor of the Ḥida's mother.

name: Hindel, daughter of Judah
desc: An ancestor of the Ḥida's mother; mother of Sarah, wife of Nathanel.

name: Sarah, second wife of Nathanel
desc: The Ḥida's great-grandmother; his mother was named after her.

name: Nathanel, head of the yeshivah of Naarden
desc: The Ḥida's great-grandfather, a pious rabbi who gave approbations to Me'il Shemu'el and the Midrash Rabbah.

name: Mindeli, first wife of Nathanel
desc: Mother of Falk son of Nathanel.

name: Hindel, the Ḥida's grandmother

patterns.rx: named Hindel(?=, who was the wife)

desc: Daughter of Nathanel and Sarah, wife of Joseph Bialer, mother of the Ḥida's mother.

name: Falk son of Nathanel, head of the court of Cleve

patterns.rx: R\. Falk(?=, son of R\. Nathanel)

desc: Husband of the Ḥida's aunt Gitli.

name: Judah, son of Gitli

patterns.rx: R\. Judah(?=, who is in Cleve)

desc: The Ḥida's cousin, a young man in Cleve.

name: Jacob Tzemaḥ
desc: Kabbalist of Jerusalem; the Ḥida saw his Meshivat Nefesh on transmigrations in manuscript in Cleve. Probably also the R. Jacob Zemah who signed the letter of the rabbis of Jerusalem on the Bnei Moshe.

name: Johanan Hanover
desc: A qatzin through whom Judah Scheyer sent the mission's money to the Ḥida in Amsterdam.

name: Moses de Raphael Mendes da Costa, gevir of Amsterdam
patterns: Signor Moses de Raphael Mendes da Costa
desc: With Isaac Teixeira de Mattos he worked for the Ḥida's mission in Amsterdam. The Ḥida's padrino on his first mission.

name: Jacob Nunes Henriques of Amsterdam
desc: A gevir of Amsterdam, one of the Ḥida's chief friends there.

name: Samuel Bueno de Mesquita of Amsterdam
desc: A gevir of Amsterdam, one of the Ḥida's chief friends there. The Ḥida's friend, brother-in-law of Medina; went with him to merchants. Took the Ḥida to the Hortus Medicus of Amsterdam, May 1778.

name: Aaron, brother of Samuel Bueno de Mesquita
desc: A friend of the Ḥida in Amsterdam.

name: Abraham da Veiga of Amsterdam
desc: A sage of Amsterdam; the Ḥida spent a Sabbath night with him.

name: David Henriques de Castro of Amsterdam
desc: A gevir of Amsterdam; the Ḥida spent a Sabbath night with him.

name: Aaron de Jacob de Prado of Amsterdam
desc: A gevir of Amsterdam; the Ḥida had the Purim meal with him.

name: Solomon, with Aaron Lombroso, of Amsterdam

patterns.rx: Signor Solomon(?= and Signor Aaron Lombroso)

desc: The Ḥida spent a Sabbath night with him and Aaron Lombroso; probably a Lombroso too.

name: Moses de Gandis of Amsterdam
desc: A sage of Amsterdam; the Ḥida spent a Sabbath night with him (the reading of the name is uncertain).

name: Moses Raphael Ḥizkiyahu da Veiga of Amsterdam
patterns: R\. Moses Raphael Ḥizkiyahu da Veiga
desc: A sage of Amsterdam, one of the Ḥida's chief friends there.

name: Isaac Saruk, son of the ḥazzan Solomon Saruk
desc: Travelled with the Ḥida by barque from Amsterdam to The Hague. Of The Hague; gave the Ḥida a fine feast and went with him on visits.

name: Aaron ha-Kohen, Sephardi of London
desc: The Ḥida lodged in his house in London, as earlier emissaries had.

name: Isaac del Valle, gevir of London
desc: A sage and gevir, head of the Ḥida's friends in London.

name: Phinehas Gomez Serra of London
desc: A friend of the Ḥida in London who took charge of the collection from individuals.

name: Jacob Kimḥi of London
desc: A great scholar in London, son of S. Kimḥi of Constantinople.

name: S. Kimḥi of Constantinople
desc: Father of Jacob Kimḥi of London.

name: Ḥayyim Albeli of London
desc: A sage in London and a friend of the Ḥida (the reading of the name is uncertain).

name: Mas'ud Bonan, emissary
desc: An earlier emissary who had to wait months in London for the council.

name: Joseph Salvador, warden of the London community
desc: A powerful warden who called the great council out of season, and the mission was paid from the general fund.

name: Joseph de Abraham Francos, gevir of London
desc: A gevir of London who took charge of the collection and to whom the English ambassador wrote; 'Signor Franco' in the same paragraph is probably the same man.

name: Mendes, gevir of London
desc: A gevir of London whom Joseph Salvador told the Ḥida to see.

name: David Castro, cantor in London
desc: The cantor in London, a friend with influence among the gevirim.

name: Jacob Rodrigues Pereira, teacher of the deaf in Paris
desc: He found the Ḥida lodging in Paris and showed him a deaf-mute boy he had taught to speak. A nobleman who came to the Ḥida's house five times; probably Jacob Rodrigues Pereira, teacher of the deaf.

name: Léon of Paris
desc: A Jew in Paris with whom the Ḥida lodged.

name: Louis XV, King of France
desc: He saw Jacob Rodrigues Pereira's pupil and granted him a yearly pension. His mistress raised Lipman Calmer to his rank.

name: Louis XIV, King of France
desc: His bronze statue in a square of Paris. His statue stands in the square of Bellecour in Lyon.

name: Henri IV
desc: His bronze statue in a square of Paris.

name: Jacob Atias, moreh of Bordeaux
desc: The aged moreh of Bordeaux who disqualified an expert shoḥet; the Ḥida settled the dispute against him.

name: Abraham Lopes of Bordeaux
desc: A learned man who examined the shoḥatim of Bordeaux with the Ḥida.

name: Abraham Monsanto of Bordeaux
desc: A learned man who examined the shoḥatim of Bordeaux with the Ḥida.

name: Benjamin Gradis of Bordeaux
desc: The only man in Bordeaux with whom the Ḥida dined, for he kept kashrut by the law.

name: Ḥayyim ha-Kohen, author of Tur Bareket and Torat Ḥakham
desc: The Ḥida prostrated himself on his tombstone in Livorno.

name: Hillel, commentator on the Sifrei
desc: The Ḥida saw his commentary on the Sifrei in manuscript in Ancona.

name: The Rif (Isaac Alfasi)
desc: His Halakhot are the pattern for the Ramban's rulings that the Ḥida saw in Reggio.

name: Ramban (Naḥmanides)
desc: The Ḥida saw his rulings on Nedarim and Bekhorot in manuscript in Reggio.

name: Trabotto family of rabbis
desc: One of the geonim of Italy whose rulings the Ḥida saw in Modena.

name: Maharshaf
desc: An earlier rabbi whose manner of preaching the Ḥida followed at Guastalla (the reading of the name is uncertain).

name: Rashbi (Simeon bar Yoḥai)
desc: The book Ari Nohem argues that the Zohar is not his.

name: Moses Ḥayyim Luzzatto
desc: The Ḥida saw in Venice the account of his affair, Gilgul Maḥloket.

name: Suleiman, disciple of the Ari
desc: He wrote the tefillin of Rashi that the Ḥida lost and found again near Padua.

name: Ḥayyim Alfandari
desc: In his book Maggid me-Reshit he praised Suleiman, the disciple of the Ari.

name: Ḥalḥul
desc: Village near Hebron whose men harassed the Ḥida on his first day.

name: ed-Dawa'ime
desc: Village where they lodged with Sheikh Nawfal.

name: Sumsum
desc: Village on the way to Gaza where they stayed in a cave.

name: Deir
desc: A camping place in the desert after Gaza.

name: Bir el-Abd
desc: Sabbath rest in the desert of Sinai.

name: Mit Ghamr
desc: Village in Egypt with four Jews and an old synagogue.

name: Bulaq
desc: River port on the way to Cairo.

name: Cairo (Miṣrayim) and Old Cairo
desc: He lodged in Cairo with Y. Manasseh and saw the Rambam's synagogue and, in Old Cairo, the synagogue of Jeremiah.

name: Rosetta (Rashid)
desc: Town in the Nile delta on the way to Alexandria.

name: Monte San Savino
desc: Town where the smiths mocked him and no one took him in.

name: Lippiano
desc: Village with five or six Jewish householders.

name: Urbino
desc: First city of the Pope's dominion on his road.

name: Argenta
desc: Town on the road from Lugo to Ferrara.

name: Finale di Modena
desc: Between Ferrara and Modena.

name: Governolo
desc: A village of gentiles before Mantua.

name: Tyrol
desc: The road from Verona to Germany, hostile to Jews.

name: Trento
desc: City of the council, where he was fined for not wearing the Jewish sign.

name: Bolzano
desc: First stop in the Tyrol; there was a synagogue for the fair.

name: Innsbruck
desc: A beautiful city with gilded palaces.

name: Pfersee
desc: Small town where Leib of Pfersee called his letters lies.

name: Kriegshaber
desc: Community bound with Pfersee.

name: Buttenwiesen
desc: A very poor village.

name: Harburg
desc: The warden there sent him off in a dung cart.

name: Oettingen
desc: The rabbi wrote him a general letter.

name: Wassertrüdingen
desc: He lodged with Wolf, warden of the province.

name: Ansbach
desc: Town and province; he achieved nothing there.

name: Wittelshofen
desc: Village in Franconia.

name: Bechhofen
desc: Village of the hard parnas Ḥayyim.

name: Lehrberg
desc: Village where the provincial rabbi Heschel lived.

name: Fürth
desc: Great community where the parnasim held him up.

name: Baiersdorf
desc: Between Fürth and Forchheim.

name: Forchheim
desc: On the road to Bamberg.

name: Buttenheim
desc: On the road to Bamberg.

name: Hirschaid
desc: On the road to Bamberg.

name: Bamberg
desc: The parnasim questioned his servant to prove him a forger.

name: Ebelsbach
desc: The Jews sent him to a gentile inn.

name: Knetzgau
desc: On the Main.

name: River Main
desc: He travelled on it from Knetzgau to Hassfurt.

name: Hassfurt
desc: He spent a Sabbath with the notable Moses.

name: Schonungen
desc: On the river Main.

name: Schweinfurt
desc: A gentile city where crowds laughed at his clothes.

name: Niederwerrn
desc: Town of the notable Zanvil.

name: Geldersheim
desc: Between Niederwerrn and Arnstein.

name: Arnstein
desc: The notable Aaron would not let him in.

name: Thüngen
desc: He slept there in a ruin.

name: Himmelstadt
desc: Village on the road to Heidingsfeld.

name: Laudenbach
desc: Village on the road to Heidingsfeld.

name: Zellingen
desc: Village on the road to Heidingsfeld.

name: Leinach
desc: Village on the road to Heidingsfeld.

name: Greusenheim
desc: Village on the road to Heidingsfeld.

name: Höchberg
desc: Village on the road to Heidingsfeld.

name: Heidingsfeld
desc: Town of the rabbi Leib Rapoport.

name: Neubrunn
desc: Between Heidingsfeld and Wertheim.

name: Wertheim
desc: Town on the Main.

name: Fechenbach
desc: Village on the Main.

name: Freudenberg
desc: Village on the Main.

name: Miltenberg
desc: Town on the Main.

name: Heubach
desc: Village on the Main.

name: Klingenberg
desc: Village on the Main.

name: Wörth
desc: Village on the Main.

name: Kleinwallstadt
desc: Village on the Main.

name: Aschaffenburg
desc: Town on the Main.

name: Seligenstadt
desc: He was helped there by the notable Leib.

name: Mainz
desc: He lodged with Eizik Gundersheim. Home of Moses Kann.

name: Hanau
desc: The rabbi Isaac at first doubted his signatures.

name: Metz
desc: Community of the rabbi Hillman.

name: Kałuszyn
desc: Community of the rabbi Wolf, brother of the rabbi of Hanau.

name: Worms (Garmiza)
desc: Ancient community where Jacob Joshua Falk confirmed his signatures; the Ḥida tells its legends.

name: Hamburg
desc: One of the three communities of Jonathan Eybeschütz; home of Wolf Hintel.

name: Altona
desc: One of the three communities of Jonathan Eybeschütz.

name: Wandsbek
desc: One of the three communities of Jonathan Eybeschütz.

name: Poland
desc: Its rabbis wrote against Eybeschütz and for Judah Yeruḥam.

name: Gernsheim
desc: Between Worms and Oppenheim.

name: Oppenheim
desc: Between Gernsheim and Mainz.

name: Bingen
desc: On the Rhine, where he met the pious Israel.

name: Sankt Goar
desc: On the Rhine.

name: Boppard
desc: On the Rhine.

name: Koblenz
desc: On the Rhine.

name: Neuwied
desc: On the Rhine.

name: Bonn
desc: On the Rhine.

name: Deutz
desc: On the Rhine, reached by boat from Bonn.

name: Cologne
desc: He travelled with men of the council of the province of Cologne.

name: Zons
desc: Village on the Rhine.

name: Düsseldorf
desc: They were not let in and spent a hungry Sabbath outside.

name: Uerdingen
desc: Village on the Rhine.

name: Moers
desc: No one took them in.

name: Rheinberg
desc: On the Rhine.

name: Xanten
desc: On the Rhine; his cousin lived there.

name: Cleve
desc: He lodged with Feibelman and met his aunt Gitli.

name: Nijmegen
desc: He heard there of the fire in Frankfurt.

name: Naarden near Amsterdam
desc: Seat of the yeshivah of his great-grandfather Nathanel.

name: Arnhem
desc: On the road to Amsterdam.

name: Amersfoort
desc: David Meldola met him there.

name: Hellevoetsluis (Alboud)
desc: Port at the edge of Holland where he took the packet boat.

name: Holland
desc: The Dutch provinces. The Dutch Republic and its province of Holland.

name: England
desc: He crossed to it in 1755.

name: Harwich
desc: Port where customs searched him; he sank in mud outside the town.

name: Tower of London

patterns.rx: the tower that they call the Tower

desc: He saw its animals, armoury and crown jewels.

name: Dover
desc: He sailed from there to Calais.

name: Calais
desc: He waited there for the carriage to Paris.

name: Blaye
desc: Reached by carriage from Paris, before Bordeaux.

name: Tomer Devorah
desc: By Moses Cordovero; he read it in Monte San Savino.

name: Tur Bareket
desc: By Ḥayyim ha-Kohen.

name: Torat Ḥakham
desc: By Ḥayyim ha-Kohen; he found it in Lippiano.

name: Sifrei
desc: He saw a manuscript commentary on it in Ancona.

name: Or ha-Ḥammah
desc: By his forefather; he saw it in manuscript in Venice.

name: Yode'ei Binah
desc: By Moses Zacuto, half printed; the press was burned.

name: Remez ha-Romez
desc: By Moses Zacuto; he saw it in manuscript in Venice.

name: Me'orot Natan
desc: Kavvanot by 'the Nasi', seen in Venice.

name: Ari Nohem
desc: A pamphlet against the antiquity of the Zohar, seen in Venice.

name: Gilgul Meḥilot (מחלו"ת)
desc: A file on the Luzzatto dispute, seen in Venice; the title is as printed, and its reading is uncertain.

name: Maggid me-Reshit
desc: By Ḥayyim Alfandari.

name: Kesef Mishneh
desc: Commentary on the Rambam, printed in Venice.

name: Ḥiddushei Halakhot
desc: He compared Joseph of Ansbach's novellae to its author's style.

name: Beit Shmuel
desc: On Even ha-Ezer; he saw it on the table of the rabbi of Hanau.

name: Pnei Yehoshua
desc: By Jacob Joshua Falk; the Ḥida saw its second part in Hanau.

name: Batei Kehunah
desc: By Isaac ha-Kohen of Jerusalem.

name: Panim Me'irot
desc: He answered a difficulty of its author.

name: Shalshelet ha-Kabbalah
desc: He thinks the legend of Rashi's mother is in it.

name: Ma'aseh Nissim
desc: The book of the wonders of the community of Worms.

name: Derishah and Sema
desc: By Joshua Falk.

name: Me'il Shemu'el
desc: Indexes and abridgement of the Shelah; his great-grandfather Nathanel gave it an approbation.

name: Meshivat Nefesh
desc: By Jacob Tzemaḥ, on transmigrations; seen in manuscript in Cleve.

name: Tzitzat Novel Tzevi
desc: Printed in secret; he saw it in Amsterdam.

name: Migdal Oz
desc: Commentary on the Rambam; he read it in the library in Paris.

name: Beit Yosef
desc: He studied it for the shoḥet case in Bordeaux. Joseph Karo's commentary on the Tur, cited on Hallel of Passover night.

name: Isaac Nunes Tavares of Bayonne
desc: Came out to meet the Ḥida at Bayonne in September 1755 and lodged him in his house. Deceased; did the Ḥida kindnesses on his first visit.

name: Samuel Alexandre Fernandes of Bayonne
desc: Son-in-law of Isaac Nunes Tavares and a dear friend of the Ḥida, who met him at Bayonne in 1755; by 1777 he was dead, and the Ḥida visited his house.

name: Jacob Levi, warden at Bayonne
desc: Warden at Bayonne who showed the Ḥida the gardens and the citadel.

name: Monsieur Casaubon of Bayonne
desc: Gentile notable at Bayonne to whom the Ḥida brought a letter of recommendation.

name: Moses ha-Kohen of Montpellier
desc: Lived at Montpellier for trade; the Ḥida spent the Sabbath with him and read his books Elim and Nishmat Ḥayyim.

name: Abraham de Roquemartine
desc: Son-in-law of Moses ha-Kohen, at Montpellier for trade; escorted the Ḥida to Lunel, and later, as rabbi and gevir of Carpentras, to L'Isle.

name: Israel, rabbi and circumciser at Nîmes
desc: The Ḥida stayed with him at Nîmes in October 1755.

name: Monsieur Vidal of Avignon
desc: Escorted the Ḥida from Avignon to Carpentras with Isaac de Monteux.

name: Samuel de Lattes, warden at Carpentras
desc: Warden who escorted the Ḥida from Carpentras to L'Isle.

name: Joseph de Beaucaire of L'Isle
desc: Head of the community of L'Isle with his sons; the main donor there.

name: Abraham de Monteux of Avignon
desc: Gevir who came from Avignon to fetch the Ḥida from Cavaillon in November 1755.

name: Moses Joseph Vidal
desc: Young gevir who escorted the Ḥida from Nice over the Colle di Tenda for ten days.

name: Jacob Astruc
desc: Escorted the Ḥida from Nice over the Colle di Tenda with Moses Joseph Vidal.

name: Simeon Mondovì of Turin
desc: Notable of Turin who showed the Ḥida kindness in January 1756. Father-in-law of Gialli.

name: Joseph Todros Ovazza of Turin
desc: Notable of Turin who showed the Ḥida kindness in January 1756.

name: Samuel Nizza of Turin
desc: Scholar of Turin who showed the Ḥida kindness in January 1756.

name: Judah Briel
desc: Author of a critique of the Gospel that the Ḥida saw in Turin.

name: Jacob Segre of Vercelli
desc: With his brother Benjamin, host of the Ḥida at Vercelli in February 1756.

name: Benjamin Segre of Vercelli
desc: With his brother Jacob, host of the Ḥida at Vercelli in February 1756. The Ḥida's host in Vercelli, August 1778.

name: Samuel Del Vecchio, rabbi of Casale
desc: Head of the court at Casale Monferrato, with whom the Ḥida had a special affection.

name: Israel ha-Kohen Vitali della Torre of Alessandria
desc: Lodged the Ḥida at Alessandria in March 1756.

name: A. ha-Levi, rabbi of Alessandria
desc: Head of the court at Alessandria who showed the Ḥida much kindness; first name given by initial only.

name: Moses Foa of Genoa
desc: Lodged the Ḥida at Genoa in March 1756; not the rabbinic judge of Senigallia of the same name. The Ḥida's host in Genoa, June 1777. The Ḥida's host in Genoa, September 1778.

name: Ḥananiah Bondi, rabbi of Livorno
desc: Rabbi of Livorno and a friend of the Ḥida, who escorted him when he left the city in 1753 and in 1757. Perhaps also the physician, the sage Bondi, who sent the Ḥida's boxes to Livorno in 1775.

name: Isaac Nunes Vais of Livorno
desc: Sage of Livorno, a friend of the Ḥida in 1756–57.

name: Eliau (Elijah) Kohen of Livorno
desc: Sage of Livorno and a friend of the Ḥida, who escorted him when he left the city in 1753 and in 1757.

name: David Medina of Livorno
desc: At his house in Livorno the Ḥida saw three air pumps.

name: A. Shapira of Livorno
desc: Rabbi who escorted the Ḥida out of Livorno in June 1757.

name: Y. Ayash
desc: Rabbi who escorted the Ḥida out of Livorno in June 1757; probably Judah Ayash of Algiers, then on his way to Jerusalem.

name: A. Segre of Livorno
desc: Ḥakham who escorted the Ḥida out of Livorno in June 1757.

name: Giovanni Caselar, ship's captain
desc: Captain of the Ragusan ship that took the Ḥida from Livorno in 1757 and was seized by a French corsair.

name: Abraham Fernandes Dias of Izmir
desc: His son and grandson met the Ḥida's ship at Izmir in July 1757 and took him home.

name: Moses Pardo of Izmir
desc: Ḥakham of Izmir, a friend, who came to the ship and lodged the Ḥida.

name: Y. Saul, rabbi of Izmir
desc: Rabbi of Izmir who honored the Ḥida in 1757.

name: Absalom ha-Levi of Izmir
desc: Ḥakham and gevir of Izmir who showed the Ḥida kindness in 1757.

name: Eliau, son of Absalom ha-Levi of Izmir
desc: Ḥakham of Izmir, son of Absalom ha-Levi.

name: Isaac Arditi of Izmir
desc: Ḥakham and gevir of Izmir who showed the Ḥida kindness in 1757.

name: A. Lapapa (probably Aaron Lapapa of Izmir)
desc: The manuscript Shitah Mekubbetset on Ketubbot that the Ḥida saw in Izmir came from him.

name: Y. Albeli
desc: Ḥakham in whose company the Ḥida left Izmir in August 1757.

name: Jacob Fernandes
desc: Travelled with the Ḥida from Izmir in August 1757.

name: Isaac Molkho
desc: Ḥakham who travelled with the Ḥida from Izmir in August 1757.

name: Moses ibn Ḥabib, rabbi of Gallipoli
desc: The Ḥida passed through Gallipoli to greet him in August 1757.

name: Isaiah Ashkenazi of Tekirdağ
desc: Great rabbi with whom the Ḥida spent a Sabbath at Tekirdağ in August 1757.

name: Samuel ha-Levi of Constantinople
desc: Official of Constantinople who lodged the Ḥida in 1757–58.

name: Moses Angel of Constantinople
desc: Son-in-law of Samuel ha-Levi, a ḥakham and gevir, who showed the Ḥida a friendly face.

name: Elijah Palombo of Constantinople
desc: Sage who went with the Ḥida to Kâğıthane on Ḥanukkah 1757.

name: Naphtali ha-Kohen of Constantinople
desc: Ḥakham who went with the Ḥida to Kâğıthane on Ḥanukkah 1757.

name: Sultan Osman III
desc: Died in October 1757 while the Ḥida was in Constantinople.

name: Sultan Mustafa III
desc: Became sultan in October 1757; the Ḥida saw his girding with the sword at Eyüp and blessed him.

name: Sultan Ahmed III
desc: Father of Mustafa III; built the kiosks at Kâğıthane.

name: Monsieur Colombo, ship's captain
desc: Captain of the French ship that took the Ḥida from Constantinople to Jaffa in 1758.

name: Israel ha-Kohen of Boğaz Hisar
desc: Ḥakham at the Dardanelles at whose house the Ḥida stayed in March 1758.

name: Jacob Zonana, çelebi
desc: Minister who built the khan at Jaffa where the Ḥida lodged in 1758; in 1764 he sent a firman about an appointment in Jerusalem.

name: Bali Babani
desc: Left Jerusalem with the Ḥida in Shevat 1764 and met Abu Ghosh on the way.

name: Moses Morpurgo
desc: Left Jerusalem with the Ḥida in Shevat 1764.

name: Abu Ghosh, chief of the outlaws
desc: Came upon the Ḥida's party on the road from Jerusalem with 250 men in 1764.

name: Shulima Albo
desc: Sage who died after a caravan was captured and tortured at Battir.

name: Raḥamim, official in Jerusalem
desc: Appointed in Jerusalem in 1764, when the seven good men of the city were removed.

name: A. Ashiao of Sidon
desc: Wrote to the Ḥida from Sidon about the firman of Jacob Zonana; name as printed.

name: Sh. Alḥadif
desc: Sage sent from Jerusalem to Jaffa in 1764 to keep the Ḥida on the mission; he went with him to Egypt that year.

name: Ḥ. Alfandari
desc: Sage sent from Jerusalem to Jaffa in 1764 with Sh. Alḥadif; printed אלפאנדאדי, probably Alfandari.

name: Y. Abulafia
desc: Rabbi who came to Jaffa in 1764 to take the Ḥida to Constantinople; after the storm he went back by land.

name: A. ben Asher
desc: A pious rabbi who was in Alexandria in 1753 and did the Ḥida much good. In 1764 he came with Y. Abulafia to take the Ḥida to Constantinople; he stayed on the ship in the storm and came back to Jaffa on Shabbat Zakhor.

name: Isaac Alshekh (Eliashar) of Hebron
desc: Sage of Hebron who travelled with the Ḥida to Egypt in 1772; printed אלישר, rendered both Alshekh and Alishar.

name: Y. Naḥmias
desc: Gevir and sage who travelled with the Ḥida from Hebron to Egypt in 1772 and spoke Turkish to the kashif.

name: Abu Dhahab, ruler of Egypt
desc: Ruler of Egypt who drove out Ali Bey; his caravan brought the Ḥida across the desert in 1772.

name: Bakir son of al-Ṣalīṭ
desc: Sheikh of the Arabs whose caravan the Ḥida joined in 1772; he asked Isaac Alshekh about Hebron's debt.

name: Sheikh al-Ṣalīṭ
desc: Arab sheikh to whom Hebron owed five thousand zolotas; captured by the pasha of Damascus.

name: Ali Bey, ruler of Egypt
desc: Mamluk ruler of Egypt who despoiled its Jews; driven out by Abu Dhahab, he died of his wounds in May 1773.

name: Aṣlan of Hebron
desc: A man of the Hebron community against whom Bakir had a claim; perhaps its agent.

name: Joseph ha-Levi Sakandari
desc: Gevir and official of Egypt killed by Ali Bey, who seized all his property.

name: Nissim, gevir of Egypt
desc: A gevir of Egypt despoiled by Ali Bey.

name: Ḥayyim Sasson
desc: A gevir of Egypt despoiled by Ali Bey.

name: Ẓāhir al-ʿUmar, ruler of Acre
desc: The rebel sheikh of Acre and Galilee, Ali Bey's ally.

name: Catherine II, Empress of Russia
desc: Ali Bey and Ẓahir sent letters to her with the commanders of the Russian fleet.

name: Murad Bey
desc: Abu Dhahab's commander who first met Ali Bey in battle in 1773.

name: Ismail Bey
desc: A bey who saved Ali Bey in the battle of 1773.

name: Jesse, gevir of Alexandria
desc: Lent the Ḥida ten reales before he sailed from Alexandria in 1773.

name: Solomon Uzan (Wazan) of Sousse
desc: Sage of Sousse who held himself to be the rabbi; offended when the Ḥida lodged with Moses Uzan. Later the qaid put him in prison over a Sabbath stew. The Hebrew name is rendered both Uzan and Wazan.

name: Judah Franco of Tunis
desc: Sage of Tunis whom the Ḥida met at Sousse and found a scholar; travelled with him to Tunis.

name: Moses Uzan of Sousse
desc: Gevir of Sousse who lodged the Ḥida in 1773.

name: Mordecai Levi of Jerusalem
desc: Emissary of the burned communities of Izmir, whom the Ḥida met at the emissaries' house in Tunis in 1773.

name: Aaron Levi of Jerusalem
desc: Father of Mordecai Levi; dead by 1773.

name: Joseph ha-Kohen, head of the rabbinic court of Tunis
desc: Sage of Tunis who came to greet the Ḥida in 1773. Brought a proof from Arakhin that the Ḥida rejects in Birkei Yosef.

name: Nathan Borgel of Tunis
desc: Sage of Tunis who came to greet the Ḥida in 1773. Sage of Tunis to whom M. ha-Levi wrote against the Ḥida (probably Nathan Borgel, who greeted him on arrival).

name: Joshua ha-Kohen Tanugi of Tunis
desc: The qaid of Tunis and the Ḥida's host there in 1773; his son Moses invited the Ḥida in his father's name.

name: Joseph Karo (Maran)
desc: His responsa Avkat Rokhel in manuscript were seen by the Ḥida in Izmir. Author of the Shulḥan Arukh, quoting the Rashba on orlah.

name: Isaac son of Malkizedek of Siponto
desc: His commentary on the Order Zera'im was seen by the Ḥida in Livorno.

name: Elijah Mizraḥi (the Re'em)
desc: The Ḥida prostrated himself on his tombstone at Eğri Kapı in Constantinople.

name: Ḥayyim Benveniste
desc: Author of the Kenesset ha-Gedolah; the Ḥida saw his responsa in Constantinople.

name: Naphtali (probably Naphtali ha-Kohen Katz)
desc: His sword and amulets were shown to the Ḥida in Constantinople.

name: Maharibal (Joseph ibn Lev)
desc: Had doubts on the case of a mamzer who purified his seed through a slave woman.

name: A. ibn Ya'ish
desc: Had doubts with the Maharibal on the case of the mamzer who purified his seed.

name: Radbaz (David ibn Zimra)
desc: Signed in agreement on the case of the mamzer who purified his seed.

name: Moses Alshekh
desc: Signed in agreement on the case of the mamzer who purified his seed.

name: Elim
desc: Book the Ḥida read at Montpellier.

name: Nishmat Ḥayyim
desc: Book the Ḥida read at Montpellier.

name: Al Tehi ka-Avotekha
desc: Epistle the Ḥida saw with a commentary in Nice.

name: Kelimat ha-Goyim
desc: Book the Ḥida saw in Turin.

name: Avon Gillayon
desc: Judah Briel's critique of the Gospel, seen by the Ḥida in Turin.

name: Or Zarua
desc: The Ḥida saw it in manuscript at Vercelli.

name: Tsevi Mudaḥ
desc: Seen by the Ḥida at Vercelli.

name: Kol ha-Remez
desc: Moses Zacuto's work, seen at Vercelli larger than the printed one.

name: Ma'amarot of Menaḥem Azariah of Fano
desc: Seen in manuscript at Vercelli.

name: Shemot (by Moses Zacuto)
desc: Book of the Remez seen in Livorno; probably his Shorshei ha-Shemot.

name: Avkat Rokhel
desc: Responsa of Joseph Karo, seen in manuscript in Izmir.

name: Shitah Mekubbetset
desc: On Ketubbot, seen in manuscript in Izmir.

name: Kenesset ha-Gedolah
desc: Work of Ḥayyim Benveniste.

name: Mishmeret ha-Mitsvot
desc: Book seen in Constantinople.

name: Megillat Sefer
desc: Its part 2 was seen in Constantinople.

name: Ḥelko shel Binyamin
desc: Book seen in Constantinople.

name: Parashat Derakhim
desc: The Ḥida read all of it on the ship from Alexandria in 1773.

name: Tosafot Yom Tov
desc: Cited by the Ḥida in Tunis on the mule.

name: Ḥavvot Ya'ir
desc: A responsum of it was the basis of the Ḥida's homily at the qaid's table in Tunis.

name: Saint-Esprit, by Bayonne
patterns: the village near Bayonne where the Jews live
desc: The Jewish village by Bayonne.

name: Peyrehorade
desc: Stop between Bayonne and Toulouse, October 1755.

name: Toulouse
desc: The Ḥida kept a Sabbath there with a poor wandering Jew in 1755.

name: Lunel
desc: Town between Montpellier and Nîmes.

name: Carpentras
desc: One of the four holy communities of the Comtat; the Ḥida preached there in 1755. Home of the Carmi brothers.

name: L'Isle(-sur-la-Sorgue)
desc: One of the four holy communities of the Comtat.

name: Cavaillon
desc: One of the four holy communities of the Comtat.

name: Rhône (river)
desc: Its flood at Avignon in November 1755 kept the Ḥida in the city. River at Lyon.

name: Spain
desc: A stone said to have been wood was sent from there to Paris.

name: Portugal
desc: Lisbon, its capital, was destroyed by the earthquake of 1755.

name: Nice
desc: The Ḥida preached there in December 1755.

name: Col de Braus and Col de Brouis
desc: Mountains crossed between Nice and the Colle di Tenda.

name: Colle di Tenda
desc: Pass crossed in deep snow on 31 December 1755.

name: Cuneo
desc: The gentiles there mocked the Ḥida's party in January 1756.

name: Fossano
desc: Stop between Cuneo and Turin.

name: Carmagnola
desc: Stop between Cuneo and Turin.

name: Vercelli
desc: The Ḥida stayed with the Segre brothers there in February 1756. Sabbath there, August 1778.

name: Casale Monferrato
desc: The Ḥida stayed with Simeon Ḥayyim Levi Morello there. The Ḥida stayed there, September 1778.

name: Alessandria (Piedmont)
desc: The Ḥida stayed there in March 1756. Visited September 1778.

name: Portoferraio
desc: Passed by sea in June 1757.

name: Piombino
desc: Passed by sea in June 1757.

name: Civitavecchia
desc: The port of Rome, passed by sea in 1757.

name: Rome
desc: Passed by sea in 1757.

name: Naples
desc: Passed by sea in 1757.

name: Sicily
desc: Passed by sea in 1757.

name: Stromboli and Vulcano
desc: The two mountains of fire seen from the ship in 1757.

name: Messina
desc: The strait passed with a Venetian pilot in 1757.

name: Morea
desc: Passed by sea in 1757.

name: Cerigo (Kythira)
desc: Passed by sea in 1757.

name: Candia (Crete)
desc: Passed by sea in 1757; in 1773 the Russian fleet lay there.

name: Archipelago (Aegean)
desc: Entered in 1757.

name: Chios
desc: Seen from the ship in 1757 and 1758.

name: Kara Burun
desc: Where a French corsair seized the Ḥida's ship in July 1757.

name: Çandarlı
desc: The corsair held the ship there six days in 1757.

name: Boğaz Hisar (the Dardanelles)
desc: The Ḥida went ashore there in 1757 and 1758.

name: Gallipoli
desc: The Ḥida greeted the rabbi Moses ibn Ḥabib there in 1757.

name: Tekirdağ
desc: The Ḥida spent a Sabbath there in 1757.

name: Sights of Constantinople
desc: Places in and around Constantinople that the Ḥida visited in 1757–58: the Yeni Han, mosques, the mint, the house of lions, the cemetery of Eğri Kapı, Eyüp, Kâğıthane and others.

name: Congregations of Constantinople
desc: Aḥrida, Yanbol, Gana, Vidia, Ḥevrah and Eliau, the synagogues the Ḥida saw in 1757.

name: Marmara
desc: Reached on the first evening from Constantinople in 1758.

name: Samos (Susam Adası)
desc: Passed by sea in 1758.

name: Kos (Istanköy)
desc: Passed by sea in 1758.

name: Patmos (Patino)
desc: The ship was held up there by a head wind in 1758.

name: Rhodes
desc: Seen from afar in 1758.

name: Cyprus
desc: Passed far off in 1758.

name: Beirut
desc: The ship took refuge there from a storm in 1758.

name: Jaffa
desc: Port of the Land of Israel, where the Ḥida landed in 1758 and was held back by storms in 1764. A companion went from Jerusalem by way of Jaffa.

name: Ramla
desc: Between Jaffa and Jerusalem.

name: Battir
desc: Village where a caravan was captured and tortured shortly before 1764.

name: Sidon
desc: Seat of A. Ashiao; taken by Ali Bey and Ẓahir in 1772.

name: Kapotkia
desc: Port the ship was making for from Jaffa in 1764; not identified.

name: Yatta and Samu
desc: Villages south of Hebron whose sheikh made trouble for the Ḥida in 1772.

name: El-Arish
desc: The Ḥida kept a Sabbath in a valley near it in 1772.

name: Gaza
desc: On the desert road to Egypt. He waited there more than fifty days in 1753.

name: Qaṭya
desc: Halt in the Sinai desert, 1772.

name: Bilbeis
desc: Town in Egypt where the kashif went in 1772.

name: Alexandria (No-Amon)
desc: The Ḥida stayed there with Signor Samuel in 1773 and sailed from it. He sailed from there to Livorno in 1753. Home of the servant Abraham Gabbai.

name: Damascus
desc: Its pasha captured Sheikh al-Ṣalīṭ.

name: Mecca
desc: Ali Bey made war on the Sharif there.

name: Acre
desc: Seat of Ẓahir, to whom Ali Bey fled.

name: Cao Dukra
desc: A cape on the sea route from Egypt westward, passed with difficulty in 1773; not identified.

name: Rigl al-Qaro
desc: Halt on the road from Sousse to Tunis.

name: Dar al-Yafriḥa, Tunis
desc: The lodging house of the emissaries in Tunis.

name: Abraham ha-Kohen (Baba Rabbi) of Tunis
patterns: R\. Abraham ha-Kohen, whom they call Baba Rabbi
desc: Earlier rabbi of Tunis, teacher of Abraham Tayyib; with Zemaḥ Tzarfati he brought the study of the Tosafot to Tunis.

name: Zemaḥ Tzarfati of Tunis
desc: Earlier rabbi of Tunis, teacher of Abraham Tayyib; Elijah was said to have healed him.

name: Nisso Joshua Nataf of Tunis
desc: Of Tunis; the Ḥida prayed on Yom Kippur 1773 in the synagogue by his house.

name: Judah Ḥayyim Raphael Nataf of Tunis
desc: Son-in-law of the qaid of Tunis, husband of Gazala; he showed the Ḥida great kindness, slept in the sukkah with him and fainted on the road to Bizerte.

name: Gazala, daughter of the qaid of Tunis
desc: Daughter of the Ḥida's host, the qaid in Tunis, and wife of Judah Ḥayyim Raphael Nataf; she showed him great kindness and gave him ten sequins.

name: Abraham Kohen, brother of the qaid of Tunis
desc: Brother of the Ḥida's host in Tunis; a kabbalist who called himself a prophet and disparaged the Ḥida. Probably of the Tanugi family, like the qaid.

name: Moses Kohen Tanugi, son of the qaid of Tunis

patterns.rx: Moses(?= \[the qaid's son\])|Moses, son of the qaid

desc: Son of the Ḥida's host in Tunis (the qaid Joshua Kohen Tanugi); took his book on astronomy and came at night to ask about the freemasons.

name: Judah ha-Kohen Tanugi of Tunis
desc: A bridegroom in Tunis who gave the Ḥida books and a silver box and escorted him to Bizerte.

name: Judah ha-Kohen Yonatan, qaid in Tunis
desc: A qaid of Tunis, relation by marriage of the Ḥida's host; died in Adar 1774.

name: Abraham ibn Asher
desc: Rabbi who went with the Ḥida to Egypt in 1764 on the way to Constantinople.

name: Y. Menasheh of Egypt
desc: Gevir and sage in Egypt who kept the Ḥida in his house for seventy days in 1764.

name: Israel Sullam of Egypt
desc: Of Egypt; held autographs of Ḥayyim Vital as a pledge and lent the Ḥida a book of practical kabbalah.

name: Joseph Bilaydo
desc: Sage in Egypt who pledged the Vital manuscripts to Israel Sullam and went bankrupt.

name: Samuel Vital
desc: Son of Ḥayyim Vital, who arranged his writings.

name: Moses Vital
desc: Son of Samuel Vital; copied the arrangement of his father.

name: Menaḥem Mir of Alexandria
desc: Of Alexandria; gave the Ḥida the Vital book on practical kabbalah and a book of astronomy that he had bought in the market.

name: Naphtali, a travelling sage
desc: A traveller whose estate was sold in Egypt with the Vital manuscript.

name: M. ha-Levi of Tunis
desc: Sage in Tunis who disparaged the Ḥida and his Sha'ar Yosef, and later in Algiers and Izmir.

name: Uziel Alhaik of Tunis
desc: Keen scholar of Tunis, opposed to emissaries, who honored the Ḥida; spelled Alhaik and Ḥaik.

name: Qaid Abraham Sadbon of Tunis
desc: Qaid in Tunis who gave large gifts; the Ḥida prayed in his congregation.

name: Samuel Sadbon of Bizerte
desc: Son of Abraham Sadbon; hosted the Ḥida in Bizerte and sent him to Livorno on his ship.

name: Judah Sadbon
desc: Merchant of the ship from Bizerte to Livorno and trading partner of the Ḥida's son-in-law; shared the lazaretto with him.

name: Shemariah Catarivas of Tunis
desc: Rabbi in Tunis who died on Rosh Ḥodesh Nisan 1774; the Ḥida eulogized him.

name: Ḥayyim Aryeh, servant
desc: Taken as the Ḥida's servant in Tunis in place of Abraham; dismissed in Livorno.

name: Samuel Fasi
desc: Gave out amulets in Tunis; the Ḥida spoke for him.

name: Ḥayyim ben Rabbi
desc: Was in Tunis; the Ḥida spoke well of him.

name: Bekhor Almosnino, emissary of Jerusalem
desc: Emissary in Tunis who claimed money from Hebron's share; the Ḥida had him sent away.

name: Raḥamim, the qaid's servant
desc: Servant of the qaid in Tunis at the Seder.

name: Abraham Kawwat of Tunis
desc: Old sage and judge of Tunis.

name: Ḥ. Lombroso of Tunis
desc: Keen scholar who died from practising letter combination; the Ḥida copied his booklet.

name: Shalom Ma'arek of Tunis
desc: Rabbi who escorted the Ḥida to Bizerte.

name: Mister Samuel, English captain
desc: Captain of the English ship from Bizerte to Livorno, 1774.

name: Joseph Leon of Livorno
desc: Gevir of Livorno who signed for the Ḥida's mission against Franco's advice.

name: Rakaḥ of Livorno
desc: Gevir who visited the Ḥida in the lazaretto.

name: Ḥ. Y. Recanati of Livorno
desc: Gevir of Livorno who signed for the mission only when the Ḥida pleaded with him.

name: Agib of Livorno
desc: Gevir of Livorno who gave 20 pieces.

name: Carvalho of Livorno
desc: Gevir who visited the Ḥida in the lazaretto.

name: A. ha-Kohen of Livorno
desc: Accompanied the Ḥida from Livorno to Pisa in 1774.

name: Abraham ha-Levi of Pisa
desc: The Ḥida's host in Pisa, 1774.

name: Count Cevoli
desc: His garden near Pisa has a "ruined machine".

name: Jacob Servi of Pisa
desc: Went with the Ḥida to Siena, 1774, and to Asciano, 1775.

name: Joshua Galico of Siena
desc: The Ḥida ate the Sabbath meal with him in Siena.

name: Mordecai Nissim of Siena
desc: Took a box round Siena for the mission.

name: David Ḥayyim Piazza of Florence
desc: Gevir of Florence who lodged the Ḥida next to his house and his room of books.

name: Gad Castil
desc: Went with the Ḥida from Florence toward Livorno, 1774.

name: Ephraim Joseph Rimini of Florence
desc: Gave the Ḥida twelve portugueses in Florence.

name: Yakar, sage in Livorno
desc: Sage in Livorno in 1775; he quarreled with the Ḥida over Hebron's debt to Damesek Eliezer, and approved Otzrot Yosef.

name: Abraham Ayash
desc: His wife sued the Ḥida before the council of Livorno.

name: Ab. Rodriguez of Livorno
desc: Pleaded for the wife of Abraham Ayash.

name: Ephraim Navon
desc: Son of the Ḥida's teacher (Jonah Navon); came from Turin about his mother-in-law's debt.

name: Elijah Naḥmu of Livorno
desc: Accompanied the Ḥida toward Pisa, 1775.

name: Isaac Conte
desc: Brought a letter of complaints from the Pereira brothers, 1775.

name: Abraham Campos of Ragusa
desc: Young relative of the Ḥida, met in Florence, 1775.

name: Menaḥem Blanes
desc: Son-in-law of David Ḥayyim Piazza of Florence.

name: Abraham ha-Levi of Pesaro
desc: Nephew of Phinehas ha-Kohen; the Ḥida stayed with him in Pesaro and made a pidyon for him when he had fever.

name: Abraham Israel, rabbi of Ancona
desc: Rabbi of Ancona who judged the Kohen gevirim's dispute with the Ḥida.

name: Matzliaḥ of Pesaro
desc: Gevir of Pesaro; in 1753 the Ḥida spent a Friday night at his house in Pesaro (printed 'Matzliaḥ of Ancona', probably the same man), and in 1775 he visited and ate with him.

name: Amron
desc: Intervened in the quarrels of Phinehas ha-Kohen and of Ferrara.

name: Morpurgo
desc: His daughter married Abraham Levi of Pesaro; he intervened in the Ferrara tax quarrel (probably the same man).

name: Gaetano, calesse driver
desc: Drove the Ḥida from Florence to Pesaro, 1775.

name: Aaron Abulafia of Ancona
desc: Chief minister of Phinehas ha-Kohen; detained by the governor of Ancona.

name: Cardinal Bufalini
desc: Ruled the province of Ancona; confined Phinehas ha-Kohen.

name: Pope Clement XIV (Ganganelli)
desc: Pope who favored Phinehas ha-Kohen.

name: David Morpurgo, slaughterer of Gradisca
desc: The Ḥida was at his son's circumcision, 1775. The Ḥida warned the town not to eat from his slaughtering, on Formiggini's word.

name: Samuel Cagli Ponente of Ancona
desc: Gevir of Ancona, brother-in-law of Phinehas ha-Kohen; gave his property to Phinehas's son Samuel.

name: Joseph Ḥai Consolo of Ancona
desc: A head of the congregation of Ancona; one of Cagli's heirs who contested the gift.

name: David ha-Kohen of Ancona
desc: Gevir of Ancona, son-in-law of Abraham ha-Kohen (his wife Reina is the sister of Phinehas) and brother of Godica. He escorted the Ḥida from Ancona in 1753; in 1775 the Ḥida made peace between him and Phinehas after twelve years of quarrel.

name: Isaac ha-Kohen of Ancona
