desc: Gevir of Cavaillon.

name: Isaiah de Bédarrides of Cavaillon
desc: The elder gevir, father of Samuel; rode with the Ḥida to L'Isle.

name: Joseph Ḥayyim Lunel
desc: Of Cavaillon.

name: Judah Ashkenazi son of Phinehas
patterns: R\. Judah Ashkenazi son of R\. Phinehas
R\. Judah son of R\. Phinehas
desc: Of Cavaillon; gave the Ḥida a silk purse.

name: Reuben of L'Isle, 'the author'
desc: Came from L'Isle with his brother; not identified.

name: Moses son of David de Milhaud, of L'Isle
patterns: R\. Moses son of the sage R\. David de Milhaud
desc: The Ḥida's host in L'Isle; his wife is the daughter of Ezekiel Carmi.

name: Moses son of Michael de Beaucaire
patterns: R\. Moses son of Michael de Beaucaire
desc: Of L'Isle; gave four louis d'or.

name: Novi
desc: The beginning of the territory of Genoa.

name: Campomorone
desc: On the road to Genoa.

name: Prague
desc: Jonathan Eybeschütz is called 'of Prague'.

name: Frankfurt am Main
desc: He stayed there more than three months in 1754 with Reuben Scheyer and Leib Wetzlar. Home of Baer Kann.

name: Moses (de) Cavaillon
desc: Partner of Ezekiel Carmi, from Beaucaire; ate with the Ḥida at Nîmes.

name: Moses son of Joseph D. M. of Carpentras
patterns: R\. Moses son of R\. Joseph D\. M\.
desc: The Ḥida's host in Carpentras in August 1777 and again at Nîmes; family name abbreviated (de Mi...), perhaps the same as Moses son of Joseph de Roquemartine.

name: Abraham, father of Mordecai Carmi
desc: Probably of the Carmi family of Carpentras.

name: Abraham Carcassonne of Avignon
desc: Escorted the Ḥida to the Rhône.

name: David Alfojit of Avignon
desc: Family name as printed; probably the Dalpuget family.

name: Joseph de Montelitz of Avignon
desc: Uncle of Joseph David Montelitz; died as the Ḥida left Avignon, September 1777.

name: Elijah Moses of Lyon
desc: Went with the Ḥida from Avignon to Nîmes. Escorted the Ḥida out of Lyon as far as La Verpillière.

name: Isaac Jesi of L'Isle
desc: Went with the Ḥida from Avignon to Nîmes, Lunel and Montpellier and showed him great kindness.

name: Judah Eliezer of Mannheim
desc: The synagogue of Nîmes was in his house.

name: Joseph Carcassonne of Nîmes
desc: Young gevir.

name: Mordecai Monte[ux]
desc: Of Nîmes; family name abbreviated, perhaps Monteux or Montelitz.

name: Jonathan ha-Kohen of Lunel
desc: He lived in Lunel; his commentary on some of the Halakhot of the Rif was seen in Florence.

name: Bezalel Alfojit of Montpellier
desc: The Ḥida's host in Montpellier, very rich and a great miser.

name: Milinda of Montpellier
desc: Founded the synagogue of Montpellier, which his widow keeps up.

name: Eliau Petit
desc: Rode with the Ḥida from Montpellier to Pézenas.

name: Gad de Bédarrides of Pézenas
desc: Received the Ḥida in his inn at Pézenas; the Ḥida made peace between him and others.

name: Michael D. R. M.
desc: Went with the Ḥida from Pézenas to Narbonne; family name abbreviated.

name: Judah de Valabrègue of Narbonne
desc: The Ḥida's host in Narbonne; probably the Signor Leon of the next day (Leon for Judah).

name: Abraham son of Gad de Bédarrides, of Narbonne
patterns: R\. Abraham son of Gad de Bédarrides

name: Vidal of Tolosa, the Maggid
patterns: Ha-Maggid(?: \[Vidal of Tolosa, author of the Maggid Mishneh\])?
desc: Author of the Maggid Mishneh.

name: Abraham Moscato of Livorno
desc: Settled in Toulouse; asked the Ḥida to deal with his wife in Bordeaux.

name: Jacob Attias of Bayonne
desc: Sage of Bayonne.

name: Abraham Nunes of Bayonne
desc: Advised the Ḥida on the mission in Bayonne; he quarrelled with his wife, deceived the Ḥida about her, and was rebuked.

name: Patto of Bayonne
desc: Invited the Ḥida in Bayonne; either Abraham or Moses Patto.

name: Abraham Patto, treasurer in Bayonne
desc: Appointed treasurer by the Ḥida.

name: Abraham Levi of Bayonne
desc: One of the heads who stood against the Ḥida; he shaved his beard on the festival and was fined.

name: Benjamin Louis of Bayonne
desc: A head of the congregation and a great miser, who stood against the mission.

name: Mordecai Lopes Fonseca, warden in Bayonne
David Levi of Bayonne
desc: Disputed a law with the Ḥida.

name: Joseph Julian of Bayonne
desc: A head of the congregation who hinted that the Ḥida's letters were false; insulted the president and was confined.

name: Moses Robles of Bayonne
desc: Rich old man of eighty who took himself for a scholar.

name: Moses Silva Valle
desc: Grandson of Isaac Nunes Tavares; bridegroom of Bereshit in Bayonne.

name: David Gomez Silva of Bayonne
desc: Invited the Ḥida to his garden; probably the same as Signor David Silva.

name: Aryeh Judah (Leon) of Modena
desc: Rabbi of Venice who came to believe in transmigration.

name: Menasseh ben Israel
desc: Author of Nishmat Ḥayyim; the text has 'Moses son of Israel'.

name: Jacob Sibbam, treasurer in Bayonne
desc: Family name as printed.

name: David Rodrigues of Bayonne
desc: Treasurer for the Land of Israel.

name: Mordecai Tama, ḥakham in Bordeaux
desc: Sage who met the Ḥida on the road and showed him manuscripts. Took great trouble for the Ḥida in Bordeaux; later he heard that Tama read Voltaire and had a concubine in America. Probably Mordecai son of Isaac Tama of Hebron, publisher of Pe'er ha-Dor (Amsterdam 1765).

name: Benjamin Abraham of Bordeaux
desc: An Ashkenazi shoḥet in Bordeaux, licensed by the rabbi of Amsterdam, who examined the knife with the Ḥida in 1755 (probably the same man). In 1777 a poor relative of Lipman Calmer, for whom the Ḥida asked Calmer to send a gift; he escorted the Ḥida out of Bordeaux.

name: Solomon Lopes, treasurer of the Portuguese community of Bordeaux
desc: Does not believe in the sages; probably a philosopher, the Ḥida says. The warden who would not reverse the council's decision on the Ḥida's mission; the Ḥida calls him a scoffer at the Sages.

name: David Lameira (Lamira) of Bordeaux
desc: Of Bordeaux; he came with the wardens and the treasurer over the community's pledge, 1777. The Ḥida went to the seven blessings of his son. The name is printed Lameira and Lamira and is not identified.

name: Rodrigues, warden in Bordeaux
desc: The Ḥida told him that he agreed to the sum the community had pledged.

name: David Attias of Bordeaux
desc: Of Bordeaux; he angered the Ḥida in November 1777, and the Ḥida sent back the almond cake he sent.

name: Isaac Lange of Bordeaux
desc: Boasted that he was God-fearing. Haggled over his pledge to the yeshivah until he signed for twenty livres a year; made a warden for the yeshivah.

name: Daniel Astruc, gevir of Bordeaux

patterns.rx: the gevir Signor Daniel|yeshivah of Signor Daniel|Signor Daniel

desc: Gevir who took the Ḥida into his house. The Ḥida's host in Bordeaux; the Ḥida preached in his yeshivah.

name: Aryeh Shealtiel
desc: Rabbi who brought news of quarrels in Livorno.

name: S. Meyuḥas
desc: Sage who quarrelled in Livorno and wanted to go to Amsterdam on a mission for Jerusalem.

name: Shem Tov ibn Gaon, author of Migdal Oz
Ḥayyim Elijah Ḥalfan
desc: Wrote against Isaac Abravanel; his quire was in Tama's book.

name: Jacob Attias, from Amsterdam, in Bordeaux
desc: Led the prayer in the Avignonese congregation of Bordeaux.

name: Jacob Azevedo of Bordeaux
desc: A heretic, with his two sons; the Ḥida got rid of him.

name: Samuel Astruc of Bordeaux
desc: Held a hundred escudos for the yeshivah, which the Ḥida collected.

name: Isaac Rubeiro of Bordeaux
desc: Had changed his name.

name: Israel Astruc of Bordeaux
desc: The Ḥida's friend in Bordeaux, who went between him and the wardens and escorted him on the road to Paris.

name: Mosinio, brother-in-law of Abraham Gradis
desc: Spoke to the council of Bordeaux for the Ḥida in the name of Abraham Gradis; the name is read so and not identified.

name: Isaac Alexandre of Bordeaux
desc: Brought the Ḥida a recommendation and three louis; probably the Signor Alexandre of the Bordeaux council.

name: Lange family of Bordeaux (Judah and Ḥayyim, sons of Mordecai)
patterns: Signor Judah and Ḥayyim, sons of Mordecai, called Lange
desc: The Ḥida drank chocolate at their house; three Lange sons escorted him out of Bordeaux.

name: Shealtiel of Bordeaux
desc: Wrote to the Ḥida what a gevir had said of him; probably of the family of the rabbi Aryeh Shealtiel of Bordeaux.

name: Samuel Pereyra of Bordeaux
desc: His stepdaughter married the son of David Lamira in November 1777.

name: Solomon Foa of Bordeaux
desc: Took the Ḥida to the son of Jacob Raphael in Bordeaux.

name: Jacob Raphael of Bordeaux
desc: His son by a noble gentile woman, circumcised in Amsterdam, put philosophical questions to the Ḥida.

name: Da Vina, officer of the yeshivah in Bordeaux
desc: With Signor Baiz he held money of the yeshivah that the Ḥida collected; the name is not identified.

name: Baiz, officer of the yeshivah in Bordeaux
desc: With Signor da Vina he held money of the yeshivah that the Ḥida collected; the name is not identified.

name: Shalom, warden of the Avignonese in Bordeaux
desc: Had withdrawn as warden over a grievance; the Ḥida persuaded him to return.

name: Solomon Petit of Bordeaux

patterns.rx: Signor Solomon(?= and Moses Petit| agreed)

desc: One of the Avignonese of Bordeaux; the Ḥida made peace between him and Jacob Naquet.

name: Moses Petit of Bordeaux
desc: One of the Avignonese of Bordeaux, brother of Solomon Petit.

name: Jacob Naquet of Bordeaux
desc: The Ḥida obtained forgiveness for him from Solomon Petit and made him apologize in the synagogue.

name: Judah Segre of Bordeaux
desc: Warden for the Ḥida's yeshivah subscriptions in Bordeaux; probably the Segre at R. Mordecai Tama's table and the Signor Segre who vowed on the road not to drink gentile wine.

name: Caleb Fonseca of Bordeaux
desc: Warden for the yeshivah subscriptions; the Ḥida annulled curses for his wife.

name: David Astruc of Bordeaux
desc: Warden for the yeshivah subscriptions; escorted the Ḥida and took on himself the three Sabbath meals.

name: Elijah Astruc of Bordeaux
desc: Escorted the Ḥida from Bordeaux and took on himself the three Sabbath meals.

name: Moses Carcassonne of Bordeaux
desc: Escorted the Ḥida out of Bordeaux.

name: Todros of Bordeaux
desc: Escorted the Ḥida out of Bordeaux.

name: Abraham Ashkenazi of Poitiers
desc: A Jew of Poitiers who had been with the Ḥida in Toulouse.

name: Reuben of Poitiers
desc: A Jew of Poitiers who had been with the Ḥida in Toulouse.

name: David Naquet, the Ḥida's host in Paris
desc: Rented rooms for the Ḥida in Paris and had him at his table; his wife was the sister of Elijah Perpignan. The Ḥida's host and beloved friend in Paris, July 1778; prays in the synagogue of the Avignonese.

name: Israel Bernard de Valabrègue, Interprète du Roi
desc: Had a royal pension as interpreter of oriental languages; the Ḥida found him a boaster who knew only the names of the sciences.

name: Mordecai Reuel of Paris
desc: Mocked by Valabrègue, he answered him with abuse.

name: Solomon Reuel of Paris
desc: The Ḥida drank chocolate at his house; he escorted the Ḥida out of Paris.

name: Mordecai Ashkenazi of Le Havre
desc: Of Havre-de-Grâce; with David Naquet in Paris.

name: Pinto, gevir in Paris
desc: Asked the Ḥida to persuade his wife to accept a get and vowed a thousand scudi for Hebron; the Ḥida refused to help separate them.

name: Israel Vidal of Paris
desc: The Ḥida would not sign a ruling on his marriage with his second wife. A companion of Israel Bernal, with a wife in Avignon, who married his maidservant.

name: Jacob Lopes Laguna
desc: A Portuguese young man in Paris who told the Ḥida that Mordecai Tama read Voltaire and believed in nothing.

name: Voltaire
desc: Mordecai Tama was said to have studied his books.

name: Jacob Goldschmidt, Ashkenazi gevir of Paris
desc: After much argument he gave the Ḥida 12 francs.

name: Solomon Perpignan
desc: Gave the Ḥida a recommendation to Lipman Nathan of Brussels.

name: Elḥanan son of Mattathias
desc: An Ashkenazi scholar who travelled with the Ḥida from Brussels to Holland.

name: Isaiah Karanfil
desc: Sent from Amsterdam by David ha-Kohen Azevedo to bring the Ḥida from Rotterdam; the Ḥida called him lazy.

name: Eizik Kohen of Rotterdam
desc: A teacher in Rotterdam who gave the Ḥida a small book he had printed.

name: Hirz, beadle in Rotterdam
desc: Beadle and trustee of the Rotterdam community, a scholar.

name: Jacob, the Ḥida's Ashkenazi landlord in Amsterdam
desc: In whose house in the Breestraat David ha-Kohen Azevedo rented two rooms for the Ḥida.

name: Yeḥiel Shalem, son of Rabbi Solomon Shalem
desc: Came to greet the Ḥida on his arrival in Amsterdam.

name: Saul son of Heschel, rabbi of Kraków

patterns.rx: R\. Saul(?=, son of the great gaon R\. Heschel)

desc: Grandfather of R. Saul Löwenstamm, in the lineage the Ḥida records.

name: Jacob of Lublin, father of R. Heschel
desc: At the head of the lineage of R. Saul Löwenstamm.

name: Ẓevi Hirsch Levin, rabbi of Berlin

patterns.rx: R\. Ẓevi(?=, head of the court of Berlin)

desc: Brother of R. Saul Löwenstamm.

name: Ḥakham Ẓevi (Ẓevi Hirsch Ashkenazi)
desc: Grandfather of R. Saul Löwenstamm and his brother through their mother.

name: Daniel Azevedo, son of David ha-Kohen Azevedo
desc: Showed the Ḥida a passage, probably at Rabbi Shalem's prompting.

name: Lobo, secretary of the Portuguese community of Amsterdam
desc: At his son's wedding Rabbi Shalem slighted the Ḥida.

name: Joseph Alvares, son-in-law of Rabbi Shalem
desc: Son of Moses Alvares and the Ḥida's close friend in Amsterdam; he gave him a Megillah and had him for the Purim meal. Probably also the Signor Alares (so printed) of 25 March 1778. Told the Ḥida of a false report about his father-in-law (Shalem).

name: Joseph di Trani (Maharit)
desc: The Ḥida cited the first part of his responsa to Rabbi Shalem; the 1885 printing reads R. Moses di Trani here.

name: Valzido, Sephardi warden and president in Amsterdam
desc: The Ḥida dined at his house in February 1778, when he was president; in April 1778 one of the three Sephardi wardens at the dedication of the new Ashkenazi synagogue. The name is printed so and not identified; the English also gives it as Alzido.

name: Samuel Ximenes, gevir of Amsterdam
desc: Gevir of Amsterdam. The Ḥida spent a Sabbath night with him in 1755 (Samuel Levi Ximenes, probably the same man). He had plotted over the rabbinate against Rabbi Shalem; probably the Signor Ximenes whose son-in-law was Jacob Teixeira.

name: Don Isaac Levi, poet
desc: Answered the Ran's lament in verse and boasted against him.

name: Makhir bar Abba Mari
desc: Author of the Yalkut ha-Makhiri, which the Ḥida saw in manuscript in Amsterdam.

name: Raphael Mendes da Costa, son of Moses Mendes da Costa
patterns: Signor Raphael de Abraham Mendes da Costa
desc: The Ḥida visited him in February 1778. Came to The Hague over the losses of Madame Patron in shares.

name: Abraham Teixeira, warden in Amsterdam
desc: Opposed the Ḥida in the Mahamad and then had a pain in his eye.

name: Moses Rodrigues, physician of Amsterdam
desc: Found the two padrinos for the Ḥida's mission, Aaron Capadose and Moses Suasso. A physician who asked the Ḥida about Capadose.

name: Emanuel Capadose, physician of Amsterdam
desc: Put philosophical questions to the Ḥida and served him at the padrino's table.

name: Isaac Fonseca, gevir of Amsterdam
desc: Father-in-law of Moses Suasso, a great shareholder.

name: The Sofiyals, travellers from Bordeaux
desc: Brought the Ḥida a letter from Abraham Gomes and news of his good name in Bayonne, Bordeaux and Paris; not identified.

name: Abraham Gomes
desc: The Sofiyals had helped him in the matter of his wife, and brought his letter to the Ḥida; the name is read so.

name: Judah de Prado of Amsterdam
desc: The Ḥida was received by his sons, the gevirim.

name: Prado of Amsterdam
desc: The Ḥida spent an evening at his house; perhaps one of the sons of Judah de Prado (the name is read so).

name: Shneyim, son of Judah de Prado
desc: The name is unclear (perhaps Senior).

name: Ado of Amsterdam
desc: Tried to arrange the Ḥida's visit to Aaron Capadose and served Rabbi Shalem at the padrino's table; the name is printed so.

name: Lindo of Amsterdam
desc: Spoke from secular books at Aaron Capadose's table, and the Ḥida answered him.

name: Aaron ha-Kohen, son of Joseph ha-Kohen of Jerusalem

patterns.rx: R\. Aaron ha-Kohen|R\. A\. ha-Kohen|R\. A\. K\.

desc: A sage in Amsterdam, appointed by Abraham Ze'evi; he had been twice to America. Probably also the R. A. ha-Kohen and R. A. K. of the initials.

name: Joseph ha-Kohen of Jerusalem
desc: Printed Divrei Yosef and his teacher Moses Galante's Zevaḥ ha-Shelamim; rabbinic teacher in Angora.

name: Moses Galante
desc: Author of Zevaḥ ha-Shelamim, printed by his disciple Joseph ha-Kohen.

name: William, servant of Aaron Capadose
desc: Walked beside the padrinos' carriage; the name is read so.

name: Solomon Levi Maduro
desc: Went before the padrinos round the doors when they collected for the Ḥida.

name: Jacob Teixeira of Amsterdam
desc: A rich miser, son-in-law of Ximenes, who signed for the mission only with trembling, for he rented Aaron Capadose's summer house.

name: Telles da Costa, gevir of Amsterdam
desc: Said that no man of honor should be the Ḥida's padrino, since he had refused to be their rabbi.

name: Niso of Amsterdam
desc: His orphans were great shareholders; his son spread slander that the Ḥida had slighted his father. The name is read so and not identified.

name: Elisha Pereira of Amsterdam
desc: A great shareholder, perhaps acting for the orphans of Niso.

name: Moses Gomeiras, warden in Amsterdam
desc: Had the Ḥida for Friday night, when the portion was read from his own Torah scroll; the name is printed so.

name: Carbon-Blanc
desc: Village where the escort from Bordeaux ate at midday.

name: Pelatzut (not identified)
desc: A village on the road north of Bordeaux; perhaps Pleine-Selve, or a pun, "an inn of horror".

name: Poitiers
desc: Where the Ḥida prayed with a minyan on the Sabbath, December 1777.

name: Dibona (not identified)
desc: A town between Port-de-Piles and Tours; perhaps Sainte-Maure or Montbazon.

name: Picquigny
desc: Lipman Calmer bought the town and its barony.

name: Ḥan Louis (Senlis)
desc: Freimann identifies the town as Senlis.

name: Péronne
desc: A customs town where the officers let the Ḥida pass on seeing the king's passport. Customs town on the road to Paris.

name: Paï (Épehy)
desc: Freimann identifies the village as Épehy.

name: Cambrai
desc: On the road to Paris, June 1778.

name: Soignies
desc: On the diligence route from Brussels to France.

name: Antwerp
desc: Sabbath there, June 1778.

name: Mechelen
desc: Town on the way from Antwerp to Brussels.

name: Brabant
desc: Austrian Brabant, under the rule of the Empress.

name: Dragaho (not identified)
desc: A village on the boat route from Rotterdam to Amsterdam.

name: Ma'adanei Melekh
desc: The Ḥida raised a difficulty against its words on tzitzit.

name: Terumat ha-Deshen
desc: Printed Haramat ha-Deshen; probably Israel Isserlein's Terumat ha-Deshen.

name: Divrei Yosef
desc: Printed by R. Joseph ha-Kohen of Jerusalem.

name: Zevaḥ ha-Shelamim
desc: By Moses Galante, printed by his disciple Joseph ha-Kohen.

name: Sha'arei Yerushalayim
desc: Probably another book printed by Joseph ha-Kohen; the text is not clear.

name: Jacob Mallekman, the Ḥida's host in Amsterdam
desc: His host in Amsterdam in 1778, who went with him on visits; family name as printed.

name: Joseph, new parnas of the Ashkenazim of Amsterdam
desc: The new parnas, whom the Ḥida visited in April 1778.

name: Leib Norbin of Amsterdam
desc: Visited by the Ḥida in Amsterdam, April 1778; name as printed (perhaps Gorbin).

name: Frinir of Amsterdam
desc: Visited with Leib Norbin in Amsterdam, April 1778; probably a family name, not identified.

name: Zanvil, son-in-law of R. Tobias
desc: Of Amsterdam, son-in-law of R. Tobias (probably Tobias Boas of The Hague).

name: Mendes, Sephardi warden of Amsterdam
desc: One of the three Sephardi wardens at the dedication of the new Ashkenazi synagogue, April 1778.

name: Abraham Fidanque
desc: Wondered why the Shulḥan Arukh has the custom of saying Hallel in the synagogue on Passover night.

name: Isaac Pasqual of Amsterdam
desc: Received the Ḥida and the Azevedos with honor, April 1778.

name: Isaac ha-Kohen Belinfante, preacher and poet of Amsterdam
desc: Poet and preacher of the Portuguese community; was writing a book of stories, poems and names of rabbis; his sermons are summarized.

name: Jacob Segal of Amsterdam
desc: A learned notable whom the Ḥida visited, April 1778.

name: David Leon, preacher of Amsterdam
desc: Preached in Portuguese in the Sephardi synagogue; two of his sermons are summarized.

name: Isaac Crasto, president of the Mahamad of Amsterdam
desc: Parnas and president of the Mahamad of the Portuguese community of Amsterdam. He signed first for the mission, for seven florins, which angered Jacob Teixeira; the Ḥida asked R. Shalem to settle the quarrels with him. The name is read so (de Crasto).

name: Abraham de Veiga, Capadose's clerk
desc: Capadose's clerk, slack in the Ḥida's affairs; probably the Signor A. D. V. of 30 April 1778.

name: Jehiel of Amsterdam
desc: Said to have spurred Abraham de Veiga to be slack in the Ḥida's affairs.

name: Joseph Bueno de Mesquita of Amsterdam
desc: Hosted the Ḥida on a Friday night with his grown children, May 1778.

name: David Bueno de Mesquita, son of Joseph
desc: Eldest son of Joseph Bueno de Mesquita.

name: Berit Yitzḥak
desc: A short, newly printed book read on the night before a circumcision.

name: Silva, ḥazzan in Amsterdam
desc: Said grace at the circumcision feast of Suasso's son, May 1778.

name: Samuel of Fraischdorf, of Eisenstadt
desc: Great-grandfather of R. Ẓevi of Bolechów; he had a maggid and was found whole in his grave years later.

name: Leib of Tzlusk
desc: In his writings, cited in Seder ha-Dorot, the Shelah is the soul of Ruth; the place is perhaps Slutsk.

name: Seder ha-Dorot
desc: Cited on the soul of the Shelah; the Ḥida corrects its reading.

name: Jacob, Abraham, Isaac and Aaron de Prado, brothers of Amsterdam
patterns: Signor Jacob, Abraham, Isaac and Aaron de Judah de Prado
desc: Gevirim, sons of Judah de Prado, who gave the Ḥida a royal table, May 1778.

name: David Meza, preacher of Amsterdam
desc: Preached for an hour that the evil inclination is called a stone.

name: David Enriques, innkeeper in The Hague
desc: The Ḥida lodged at his inn in The Hague, May 1778.

name: Moses de Pinto, warden in The Hague, son-in-law of Moses de Pinto
desc: Showed the Ḥida his rich furniture; his father-in-law had the same name.

name: Abraham Boas, son of Tobias Boas
desc: Of The Hague; told the Ḥida about China and the lost tribes in America, and took him to Scheveningen.

name: Simeon Boas of The Hague
desc: Visited by the Ḥida in June 1778; probably a son of Tobias Boas.

name: Abraham Nancy, teacher in the house of Tobias Boas
desc: A rabbi in The Hague, teacher in the house of R. T. B.

name: Hilman, teacher of Moses Lehren
desc: The "sharp gaon" whose pupil Moses Lehren was.

name: Abraham ha-Kohen Faro Salazar of The Hague
desc: Gave four florins, showed bladder stones and a portrait of Jacob Sasportas.

name: Jacob Sasportas
desc: His portrait was shown to the Ḥida in The Hague.

name: Neḥemiah the barber
desc: Walked with the Ḥida in the wood of The Hague.

name: Joseph della Reina
desc: Named as a practitioner of practical kabbalah in the stories of the Baal Shem of London.

name: Judah the Pious (Judah he-Ḥasid)
desc: Named with Joseph della Reina in the stories of the Baal Shem of London.

name: Ḥesheq Shelomo
desc: Manuscript of customs and responsa by the ḥazzan Solomon Saruk of The Hague.

name: Eliezer Kann, son of Baer Kann of Frankfurt

patterns.rx: R\. Eliezer(?=, son of R\. Baer Kann)

desc: A notable of The Hague; sent a cake and visited the Ḥida in Rotterdam with his wife and son.

name: Täubchen, wife of Eliezer Kann
desc: Came with her husband to see the Ḥida in Rotterdam.

name: Benjamin Teixeira of The Hague
desc: Sent his carriage and showed the Ḥida his large garden.

name: Simeon Kann, grandson of Moses Kann of Mainz
desc: Of The Hague; son of Leib Kann; gave a secret donation for Hebron and a gift for Birkei Yosef.

name: Moses Kann of Mainz
desc: Grandfather of Simeon Kann.

name: Leib Kann, son of Moses Kann

patterns.rx: R\. Leib(?= son of R\. Moses Kann)

desc: Father of Simeon Kann.

name: Isaac Aboab (da Fonseca)
desc: The old rabbi of Amsterdam in the days of the Peri Ḥadash.

name: Isaac de Aaron Suasso, parnas of The Hague
desc: The parnas in whose house the Pintos and Suassos gathered, June 1778.

name: Aaron de Moses de Pinto, gabbai of The Hague
patterns: Signor Aaron de Moses de Pinto
desc: The gabbai, who paid the doorkeepers of the Prince's cabinet and gave a table of sweets.

name: Moses de Aaron de Pinto of The Hague
patterns: Signor Moses de Aaron de Pinto
desc: Served the Ḥida liqueurs and showed him his Torah scroll; brother of Joseph de Pinto.

name: Joseph de Pinto of Amsterdam
desc: Came from Amsterdam to The Hague, June 1778; brother of Moses de Aaron de Pinto.

name: Costa Athias
desc: Came to The Hague over the losses of Madame Patron in shares.

name: Madame Patron of The Hague
desc: A rich childless widow who lost her fortune and more in shares, 1778.

name: Rachel, innkeeper in Rotterdam
desc: A widow with whom the Ḥida lodged near the synagogue in Rotterdam.

name: Girzoni, son-in-law of Rachel of Rotterdam
desc: Kept the inn in the Boompjes, Rotterdam, with his mother-in-law; name as printed.

name: Ḥayyim Breslau of Rotterdam
desc: An outstanding scholar of Rotterdam who visited the Ḥida and studied with him.

name: Ber Kokish of Rotterdam
desc: Brother-in-law of Tobias Boas; once head of the Ashkenazim in Amsterdam, he lived modestly in Rotterdam after his son's losses.

name: Israel bar Ezekiel of Rotterdam
desc: Organized the outing to Delft and gave gifts, June 1778.

name: Peretz, beadle and trustee of Rotterdam
desc: The beadle and trustee of the Rotterdam community, who collected for the mission.

name: Isaac Selig of Rotterdam
desc: A worthy young man, called son of R. Peretz and also son of R. Solomon; accompanied the Ḥida on the boat.

name: Leib, son of Peretz of Rotterdam
desc: On the outing to Delft, June 1778.

name: Erasmus
desc: The Ḥida saw his statue in Rotterdam and retells a local story about him.

name: Wolf, young man of Rotterdam
desc: Visited the Ḥida on a Sabbath in Rotterdam.

name: Silva of Rotterdam
desc: Visited the Ḥida on a Sabbath in Rotterdam.

name: Samson, parnas of Rotterdam
desc: A parnas visited with Moses Springer.

name: Man, new parnas of Rotterdam
desc: The new parnas, with whom the Ḥida had a Sabbath meal.

name: Jacob de Prins of Rotterdam
desc: Received the Ḥida with honor; the name is uncertain.

name: Anshel of Rotterdam
desc: Brother-in-law of R. Eliezer; on the outing to Delft.

name: Solomon son of Wolf, of Rotterdam
patterns: R\. Solomon son of the rabbi Wolf
desc: On the outing to Delft, June 1778.

name: Jacob Hamburg of Rotterdam
desc: Visited by the Ḥida, June 1778.

name: Zelig, travelling companion to Brussels
desc: Kept the Sabbath with the Ḥida in Antwerp and travelled with him to Brussels; quarrelled with Abraham.

name: Lipman bar Nathan, parnas in Brussels
desc: An Ashkenazi parnas in Brussels. In 1778, on the way north, he said he had no room for the Ḥida and then complained that he had not come to eat; on the way back he hired places for him in the diligence and brought him to his house.

name: Ḥananel de Milliav (Vidal père et fils) of Paris
desc: Of Paris; he took the Ḥida to Lipman Calmer, had a synagogue in his house, arranged the diligence to Lyon, and gave a recommendation to the inn at Chalon. Also called Vidal père et fils; the family name is printed Milliau and Milliav (perhaps Milhaud).

name: Abraham Léon of Bayonne
desc: A young man from Bayonne who had served the Ḥida there; in Paris in 1778.

name: Israel Bernal of Paris
desc: Visited the Ḥida in Paris, full of his own praises.

name: Aaron Ronit of Paris
desc: Told the Ḥida of the abominations of Paris and confessed his sins.

name: Silveira of Paris
desc: Accompanied the Ḥida to the diligence on leaving Paris.

name: Nimmukei Rid on the Pentateuch
desc: Manuscript the Ḥida copied in the king's library in Paris.

name: Benjamin Naquet of Lyon
desc: Met the Ḥida's boat at Lyon.

name: Manasseh de Bizes of Lyon
desc: Received the Ḥida at Lyon; the Ḥida found him stingy over the doctor's costs.

name: Reuben Moses of Lyon
desc: Received the Ḥida at Lyon; a great miser, the Ḥida says.

name: Abraham Perpignan of Lyon
desc: Brother of Elijah (Elia) Perpignan; invited the Ḥida to his house in Lyon.

name: Guastalla, a young man of Turin
desc: Warned the Ḥida in Lyon about the Turin customs; met him at Turin; probably the same young man.

name: Aaron Reuel of Lyon
desc: With the Ḥida in Lyon, July 1778.

name: Benjamin de Monteux
desc: Very rich; father-in-law of Azriel Carmi. Surname also written Montélis, Montel, Monteux: his daughter Léa Montel married Azariel Crémieux at Carpentras, 23 March 1776 (J.-C. Cohen, genealogy).

name: Azriel Carmi
desc: Brother of Solomon and Mordecai of Carpentras; a gambler who lost six thousand francs. In French records Azariel Crémieux; married Léa Montel, daughter of Benjamin, at Carpentras on 23 March 1776 (J.-C. Cohen, genealogy).

name: Solomon Carmi of Carpentras

patterns.rx: R\. Solomon(?= and R\. Mordecai of Carpentras)

desc: Brother of Azriel and Mordecai Carmi.

name: Azariah Vidal, cantor in Lyon
desc: The cantor of the new synagogue in Lyon, a bridegroom, who took the Ḥida to the baths.

name: Perrache
desc: "A philosopher" who drove back the Rhône at Lyon and made new land.

name: Samson Franquet of Lyon
desc: Asked to help pay the Ḥida's doctor in Lyon; name as printed.

name: Moses de Alpuget of Lyon
desc: Asked to help pay the Ḥida's doctor in Lyon.

name: Menaḥem Fubini, gevir of Turin
desc: The Ḥida's host and friend in Turin, 1778; helped settle the debt quarrel.

name: Israel Malvano of Turin
desc: Preached in the yeshivah of Turin, August 1778.

name: Joseph Yarak of Turin
desc: Of Turin; with him the Ḥida spoke about the mission and the compromise.

name: Solomon Jona, rabbi of Turin
desc: Rabbi of Turin; pleaded for Abraham and drew up the compromise deed.

name: Ephraim of Turin, son of the Ḥida's teacher
desc: Quarrelled with the Ḥida over his mother-in-law's debt and obtained a sequestration on the Hebron money.

name: Morino of Turin
desc: One of the arbiters of the debt quarrel; perhaps "our teacher" (the rabbi).

name: Hezekiah Pescarol of Turin
desc: A man of sense, one of the arbiters; the prime minister sent for him about the Ḥida's passport.

name: Joḥanan Ẓevi Kaziggin of Turin
desc: Preached in the yeshivah of Turin; signed himself "Bor Ẓaki".

name: Abraham son of Y. D. Treves, of Turin

patterns.rx: Signor Abraham(?=, son of Y\. D\.)

desc: Son-in-law of the sage R. D. Rakaḥ.

name: D. Rakaḥ, sage of Turin
desc: A late sage, father-in-law of Abraham Treves.

name: Gialli of Turin
desc: Son-in-law of Simeon Mondovì.

name: Menaḥem Bachi, beadle of Turin
desc: Invited the Ḥida to chocolate.

name: Mordecai ha-Levi of Turin
desc: Invited the Ḥida with the rabbi.

name: Clotilde of France, Princess of Piedmont
desc: Sister of Louis XVI, married to the Prince of Piedmont; the Ḥida brought her a letter from Madame Adélaïde, and she ordered that he be given a passport.

name: Meir Bachi
desc: A young sage who went with the Ḥida from Turin to Casale; probably the R. M. Bachi of Casale.

name: S. Bachi, rabbi of Casale
desc: An old rabbi of eighty-five in Casale, 1778.

name: Benjamin Pitigliano de Lattes
desc: Escorted the Ḥida ten miles out of Turin at Fubini's order.

name: Elijah Ghediglia
desc: A sage met on the road to Vercelli, going to Turin.

name: Jehiel Ḥayyim Treves, rabbi of Vercelli
desc: Rabbi of Vercelli.

name: Jacob Abraham Pugliese of Vercelli
desc: Son-in-law of Y. Formiggini; gave the Ḥida a feast and an agate snuffbox.

name: Mordecai Treves
desc: A gevir who accompanied the Ḥida from Vercelli to Casale.

name: Isaac Ḥayyim Kohen Cantarini
desc: A gevir, brother-in-law of Mordecai Treves; accompanied the Ḥida to Casale.

name: Simeon Ḥayyim Levi Morello, gevir of Casale
desc: Notable of Casale Monferrato who lodged the Ḥida in 1756 and escorted him toward Alessandria; in 1778 again his host, who feasted him every day.

name: Bathsheba, wife of Simeon Morello
desc: Of Casale.

name: Zipporah, daughter of Simeon Morello
desc: Of Casale; wife of Meir Zalman Vitta.

name: Meir Zalman Vitta of Casale
desc: Son-in-law of Simeon Morello and son of Joḥanan Vitta.

name: Joḥanan Vitta of Casale
desc: Father of Meir Zalman; gave his share of the family endowment to the Land of Israel.

name: Abraham Luzzatto of Casale
desc: A sage, secretary of Simeon Morello, who went with the Ḥida to Alessandria.

name: Abraham Pavia of Casale
desc: Brother-in-law of Menaḥem Fubini.

name: Samuel Pavia of Casale
desc: Partner of Simeon Morello.

name: Sabbatai Zalman Vitta of Casale
desc: Gave the Ḥida no satisfaction.

name: S. D. Mi-Zekenim of Casale
desc: A ḥaver visited by the Ḥida in Casale.

name: Solomon Fubini, warden of Casale
desc: Visited by the Ḥida on the Sabbath in Casale.

name: Elijah (E.) ha-Levi, rabbi of Alessandria
desc: Showed the Ḥida his books "Eliyahu in four"; argued for the individuals who gave little.

name: Kursaya de-Eliyahu, Tayya'a Eliyahu, Eliyahu Kotev, Seder Eliyahu and Saba Eliyahu

patterns.rx: Kursaya de-Eliyahu|Tayya'a Eliyahu|Eliyahu Kotev|Seder Eliyahu|Saba Eliyahu

desc: The manuscript works of the rabbi of Alessandria.

name: Azriel Amar
desc: Son of the innkeeper at Alessandria, who offered to serve the Ḥida as far as Genoa.

name: Gershon della Torre, warden of Alessandria
desc: Gave six lire, which the Ḥida returned; escorted him out of Alessandria.

name: Israel Pugliese of Alessandria
desc: Sent a sequin after the Ḥida's protest.

name: Hillel bar Solomon Vitali, warden of Alessandria
desc: Offered sweets for his daughter's betrothal.

name: Azriel Joel ha-Kohen of Alessandria
desc: An officer, father of seven daughters; the Ḥida was at the naming of the seventh.

name: Manuel, son of Moses Foa of Genoa
desc: Went with the Ḥida to the Porto Franco.

name: Sipolina of Genoa
desc: Held the trunk sent from Lyon in the Porto Franco.

name: Solomon Franco Miranda
desc: A young man who joined the Ḥida from Genoa to Lerici.

name: Cava of Pisa
desc: The Ḥida, his son and grandson stayed with him in Pisa, 1782.

name: Emmanuel Valensi
desc: Servant of the Ḥida's son Abraham, 1783.

name: Samuel Sanguinetti, brother-in-law of Abraham Azulai
desc: Son of Rabbi A. Sanguinetti; came out of the lazaretto in 1783 and travelled with Abraham to Modena.

name: Abendana of Pisa
desc: The Ḥida lodged in his house in Pisa, 1784.

name: Bella, the Ḥida's maidservant
desc: Went with the family to Pisa, 1784.

name: Ḥ. H. Tubiana
desc: Sailed with Abraham Azulai to Tunis, 1784.

name: Leiden
desc: On the barge from Amsterdam to The Hague, May 1778.

name: Leidschendam
desc: Village on the way from Leiden to The Hague.

name: Scheveningen
desc: Seaside village near The Hague, visited June 1778.

name: Eisenstadt
desc: Home of Samuel of Fraischdorf.

name: Delft
desc: Outing from Rotterdam, June 1778.

name: Zeeland
desc: Province of the Dutch Republic, crossed by boat to Brabant.

name: Lillo
desc: Village at the edge of the Dutch Republic.

name: Middelburg
desc: In Zeeland, on the sea route to Brabant.

name: Pelipo
desc: Place at the beginning of Brabant, on the way to Antwerp; not identified.

name: Pont-Sainte-Maxence
desc: Stop on the road to Paris.

name: Lyon
desc: The Ḥida stayed there, ill, July–August 1778.

name: Chailly
desc: Stop on the diligence from Paris.

name: Pont-sur-Yonne
desc: Stop on the diligence from Paris.

name: Joigny
desc: Stop on the diligence from Paris.

name: Vermenton
desc: Stop on the diligence from Paris.

name: Houvrai
desc: Village on the diligence route from Paris.

name: Arnay-le-Duc
desc: Stop on the diligence from Paris.

name: Chalon
desc: Sabbath there before the boat to Lyon.

name: Mâcon
desc: Night on the boat journey to Lyon.

name: Reyssouze
desc: Village on the Saône where they had a meal.

name: Saône
desc: River at Lyon.

name: Geneva
desc: Guastalla went there from Lyon.

name: Basel
desc: Where Erasmus died.

name: Savoy
desc: Crossed on the way from Lyon to Turin.

name: La Verpillière
desc: Village where the Lyon escort turned back.

name: La Tour-du-Pin
desc: On the road from Lyon to Savoy.

name: Pont-de-Beauvoisin
desc: Frontier of France and Savoy.

name: Chambéry
desc: City of Savoy, August 1778.

name: Aiguebelle
desc: Town in Savoy.

name: Laniza
desc: Village in the Maurienne; not identified.

name: Digibil
desc: Village in the Maurienne; not identified.

name: La Chapelle
desc: Village in the Maurienne.

name: Saint-Jean-de-Maurienne
desc: Town in Savoy.

name: Modane
desc: Village below Mont Cenis.

name: Mont Cenis
desc: The pass from Savoy to Piedmont, crossed in a chair.

name: Lanslebourg
desc: Village at the foot of Mont Cenis.

name: Novalesa
desc: Village at the foot of Mont Cenis in Piedmont.

name: Sant'Ambrogio
desc: Last night before Turin.

name: Chivasso
desc: First night out of Turin.

name: Dora
desc: River crossed by ferry on the way to Vercelli.

name: Voltaggio
desc: On the road to Genoa.

name: Bocchetta
desc: The pass to Genoa.

name: Lerici
desc: Reached by felucca from Genoa.

name: Massa
desc: Stop on the post road to Pisa.

name: Stagno
desc: Near Livorno, where his son-in-law met him.

name: Lucca
desc: The baths in its mountains, 1782.
